stories.title: MMBets: The Memphis Grizzlies are going to be scrappy
stories.summary: The Mavericks will not have fun dealing with this team
stories.detailText: The Memphis Grizzlies are in full rebuild mode. Their young duo of the last seven years is completely gone. Ja Morant was shipped to Portland, Jaren Jackson Jr. was traded to Utah, and Memphis now has its eyes set on the draft picks they made over the last few seasons. Cameron Boozer from Duke and Cedric Coward highlight their exciting new core, but guys like Jaylen Wells and Zach Edey have shown promise as well. Memphis has just four players on its roster with over three years of NBA experience. Having direction in the NBA is a good thing. There are some teams stuck on their sunk costs. Memphis is not one of those teams. 2027 will be a learning year for both their young players and their inexperienced coach, Tuomas Iisalo. Expectations for the Grizzlies are low, but their talent could surprise a lot of people. Memphis Grizzlies: Over/Under 30.5 wins (-110/-115) To win the NBA Finals: +100000 Last Season: 25-57, missed playoffs Key Additions: Cameron Boozer, Quentin Post, Jerami Grant. Isaiah Stewart Key Losses: Ja Morant, Jaren Jackson Jr., Kyle Anderson, Santi Aldama Mavericks fans should be very familiar with this Memphis team. They beat the Mavericks three times last season, all by double digits. Cedric Coward, Scotty Pippen Jr., Jaylen Wells, and Zach Edey all had good games against Dallas and now return a year better. Boozer looks to be one of the most ready and NBA-conditioned skill sets out of this draft and will contribute right away. They have a high-energy, young group that will get after it on defense and move the ball on offense. Jerami Grant is a seasoned veteran who has won a lot of meaningless games in his career. Isaiah Stewart will give this team a percentage of the edge that the old grit-and-grind Grizzlies used to play with. I don’t see this scrappy team as a bottom-feeder in the West. Getting to 35 wins is not out of the question. Prediction: Over 30.5 wins (-110)

stories.title: Former Warriors No. 2 pick Wiseman plays way onto New York Knicks roster
stories.summary: The Knicks cut Bruce Brown and appear to be selecting the former Warriors No. 2 overall pick for their last roster slot.
stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 5: James Wiseman #35 of the New York Knicks in action against the Philadelphia 76ers during a preseason game at Xfinity Mobile Arena on October 5, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The 76ers defeated the Knicks 120-97. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images James Wiseman almost gave up on the NBA. Now he’s on the opening night roster for the defending champs. The Knicks invited a number of veterans to compete for the last spot on their roster, an approach that worked well last season when Landry Shamet emerged from a crowded field to become one of the team’s most important bench players. Wiseman beat out John “Jitty” Konchar, Ochai Agbaji, Tony Bradley and Bruce Brown, while his competition at center, Drew Eubanks, tore a pectoral muscle and got waived. Now Wiseman steps in as the third center for the Knicks, behind Karl-Anthony Towns and rebounder supreme Andre Drummond. He’s in a very different position than he was when the Warriors selected him with the No. 2 pick in the 2020 draft, having had his career derailed by injuries. Wiseman wasn’t a good fit as a raw rookie who played just three games in college before turning pro, trying to find his place on a veteran team that had championship aspirations. His pandemic-shortened rookie season had virtually no training camp, then he suffered a meniscus tear that cost him the end of the year and all of his sophomore season. Golden State eventually traded him to the Detroit Pistons in 2023, more to ditch his salary than anything else. The Pistons had a glut of young centers and Wiseman again had trouble getting playing time. It looked like he had found a home with the Indiana Pacers in 2024, only to tear his Achilles in the first game of the season. Why is he getting another chance in New York? The answer is head coach Mike Brown, who had experience coaching Wiseman with the Warriors and called him a “fantastic human being.” Wiseman is still just 25 years old, younger than both Quinten Post and Charles Bassey and only a year-and-a-half older than Yaxel Lendeborg. He has a fantastic chance to rebuild his career, especially if he can win over Tracy Morgan, Timothee Chalamet, and Spike Lee. Wiseman’s NBA future may depend on him turning into a solid shot-blocker and rebounder, who can be a reasonable threat as a perimeter shooter. He should get chances to prove himself, as Towns is going to play a lot of minutes at power forward, and the 33-year-old Drummond is no longer the iron man he used to be. The limited, specific role the Knicks need from Wiseman might just be what he needs to establish himself as a reliable backup big. It’s a tiny role on an extremely famous team, and one that could showcase Wiseman, not necessarily as a future star, but as a competent NBA center, After all, Wiseman has played only 152 games in a six-year NBA career, which is only five more than Gui Santos. And while he hasn’t found success on the court, Wiseman has never been a jerk — he just keeps getting hurt. For the Knicks, it’s a calculated gamble for a team with very little financial wiggle room. While Wiseman is officially the third center, the potential upside of Wiseman, especially when playing with someone like Jalen Brunson, is quite intriguing. The Knicks only need Wiseman to be an adequate backup center. If he provides more than that, it’s a huge bonus for the defending champions. Three years ago, would you have believed that James Wiseman was closer to winning an NBA title than Steph Curry? This is the world we’re living in.

stories.title: Pistons season preview: Kevin Huerter’s 3-point shooting could make or break his spot in the rotation
stories.summary: Kevin Heurter provides a lot of skills to the Pistons, but recapturing his shooting is the most important.
stories.detailText: When the Detroit Pistons traded Jaden Ivey at the deadline last season for Kevin Heurter, I was a bit underwhelmed. I hadn’t spent a ton of time watching Heurter play throughout his career and pretty much just viewed him as a shooter whose shot had been failing him the last couple seasons. Say what you want about Jaden Ivey and where things have gone for him since that trade, but getting that value out of somebody you spent the 5th pick on just a few years earlier could be viewed as selling low. Especially since that player had seemingly lost the one skill that he had banked on throughout their career, and Ivey was in the midst of a breakout season before suffering his season-ending injury the prior season and was still hypothetically getting his legs back when dealt. When Heurter arrived, the shooting was mostly still dormant, but what stood out was all of the little things on the court he was able to do. His finishing around the basket is fantastic, and he can defend well in a team setting. I wouldn’t call him a shot-creator, but he does have some ability to put the ball on the floor and create a little offense for himself and others, especially when playing off of another ball handler, a skillset the Pistons badly need. All of these things are why he was given a three-year, $27 million deal to return to the team in the offseason. Those are the things that still have value for a bench player, even if his shot never gets back to where it was early in his career. But as the Pistons look to keep their reign at the top of the Eastern Conference, they will need bench players who can provide skills their main rotation players do not, and one of those skills is outside shooting. If Kevin Heurter hopes to carve out a consistent role in the Pistons’ regular-season rotation, getting his shot back is going to make or break his season. The Shooting Kevin Huerter is a 36.8% three point shooter for his career. But that is skewed heavily by four of his first five seasons in which he shot over 38% from beyond the arc, which is also where he got his reputation as a shooter. After hitting a career-high 40.2% of his outside shots as a key member of the 2022-23 Sacramento Kings that ended the season as the 2-seed, his shooting has fallen off a cliff. He shot 36.1% during the 2023-24 season, still a solid number. However, he only shot 33.8% from beyond the arc in 2024-25 with both the Kings and Bulls. Then, he shot 30.8% last year with both the Bulls and Pistons, but only 29.4% with the Pistons. It was a small sample size, and he was trending up a bit towards the end of the season before a hip injury kept Heurter out for most of the playoffs. Heurter actually got minutes in game 1 of the playoffs and appeared like he was going to be a part of JB Bickerstaff’s playoff rotation, so the timing of his injury was unfortunate. Heurter reportedly underwent a procedure to clean up this injury, which had been bothering him for most of last season, so maybe being fully healthy will help get his shooting back on track. The reason why Huerter has stuck around in team’s rotations the last couple seasons despite the drop-off in shooting are the things I listed above, like his finishing ability and his ability to do the tertiary things that may not show up on a box score. Huerter has shot 75% or above from 0-3 feet since the 2022-23 season with the Kings. He has actually been above 80% from that range the last couple of seasons. That is a very solid number for any player, but especially one who has the reputation as a one-dimensional shooter. However, over 50% of his shots still come from beyond the arc, which is why recapturing his early-career shooting ability is so crucial. The Pistons spent the offseason acquiring more players who can put the ball in the basket from beyond the arc. With their young core of Cade Cunningham, Ausar Thompson, and Jalen Duren locked in, the Pistons are positioned well to be a very good regular-season team for the foreseeable future. But, two of those three are not outside shooters, so surrounding them with guys that can shoot is almost as important as getting a secondary offensive option that can take some creation pressure off of Cade Cunningham. You know that guys like Isaiah Joe, Duncan Robinson, and even John Collins are going to shoot in the high-30s and low-40s from beyond the arc, as that is something they have done for at least the last 3 or 4 years. In the case of Kevin Heurter, you don’t have that same level of trust because of how much the shooting has fallen off over the last couple of seasons. You also still have players getting rotation minutes beyond the “Big Three,” like Ron Holland, who are still a work in progress from beyond the arc. So, having a player like Kevin Heurter come off the bench and return to being the 38%+ shooter he was early in his career could be a boon to the Pistons’ rotation. It would also make the contract he signed in the offseason very good value since he does do other things on the basketball court well. The Pistons don’t need another one-dimensional offensive player who can score inside and play a little defense. They need guys that can hit shots from outside, so Cade Cunningham, Ausar Thompson, and Jalen Duren can attack the basket and dominate games inside like they did all last year. Kevin Heurter, at his peak, can provide exactly that while also being able to put the ball on the floor a bit, finish inside, and not get played off the floor defensively. The Verdict JB Bickerstaff seems to trust Kevin Heurter regardless of whether or not he is hitting outside shots. That is evidenced by the fact that he was in the playoff rotation last season before his injury. But, the Pistons did add some more backcourt players in the offseason that will fight for minutes like Ebuka Okorie and Isaiah Joe. Heurter has a size advantage over those two and has the positional versatility to play minutes at the three. The Pistons also have a few players who will see minutes at the three like Duncan Robinson, Ron Holland, and Javonte Green. Heurter probably can’t reach the level of defense of a Holland or Green or the level of shooting of Duncan Robinson, but some of his complementary skills can be very useful if he is able to get back to form from beyond the arc. He can be somebody who puts some of the skills of both groups of players into one body and can kind of split the difference between all of these likely rotation mainstays. I don’t see a season quite as good from beyond the arc as he was at his peak, but even getting back to that 2023-2024 season shooting of 36.1% from beyond the arc will be a huge help to the Pistons and give a reason for JB Bickerstaff to continue giving minutes to Heurter.

stories.title: Will the Suns win a playoff series? Mat Ishbia thinks so
stories.summary: Mat Ishbia or Mat Wishbia?
stories.detailText: Mat Ishbia is confident about the Phoenix Suns escaping the first round of this year’s playoffs. Is this fake-it-till-you-make-it internet bluster or are the Phoenix Suns built for playoff success? Phoenix Suns owner Mat Ishbia predicts team will win opening round playoff series — and the NBA season hasn't even started https://t.co/tzmxG6mttK — CNBC (@CNBC) October 16, 2026 It wouldn’t be the first time Ishbia expressed his confidence in the potential of the Phoenix Suns. To open the 2025-26 season, The Ringer predicted the Suns’ defense to finish at the bottom of the league, an assertion that Ishbia vehemently rejected. The Suns stamped his words with an exclamation point, finishing in the top 10 in defensive rating. Can the Suns do it a second time and deliver Phoenix its first playoff series win after three years of disappointment? The answer to that may depend on who they play. The following are my predictions of how the Suns might fare against the presumptive top 6 teams in the Western Conference in a seven-game playoff series. Suns 0 – Thunder 4 The Thunder are the team that the Phoenix Suns are building to be. It was very clear in last year’s playoff matchups that the Thunder consistently turned aggressive defensive pressure on the perimeter and active hands into turnovers that sparked eight- to twelve-point runs. That’s exactly what the Suns have described this iteration of the roster to become over the course of the remaining years of Booker’s contract. I don’t think they get there this season. If the Suns want to avoid another first-round exit, they must avoid the play-in and the Thunder. Suns 2 – Spurs 4 SAN ANTONIO, TEXAS – APRIL 28: Victor Wembanyama #1 of the San Antonio Spurs celebrates with teammates after the victory against the Portland Trail Blazers in Game Five of the First Round of the NBA Western Conference Playoffs at Frost Bank Center on April 28, 2026 in San Antonio, Texas. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Ronald Cortes/Getty Images) | Getty Images If there’s anything the preseason has shown us, it’s that the Suns have the Spurs number. Despite this, I think handling Wemby, in the manner in which the Suns have been able to contain him, takes its toll, and the supporting cast of Castle, Harper, Fox, and the refs are going to prove to be too much for the Suns to take down. However, I don’t think they go quietly into the night in this scenario and score at least two wins in a six-game scuffle. *In the event of a Wemby-less Spurs. Suns 4, Spurs 1. Last year, Victor Wembanyama played a total of 1,866 minutes in the regular season. He went on to play an additional 750 minutes in the Spurs’ Finals run, totaling 2,616. In his rookie year, he totaled 71 games played and 2,106 minutes. He followed up with 1,527 minutes and 46 games played his sophomore season. If Wemby struggles to stay on the court, expect a very different playoff experience from the Spurs this season. Suns 1 – Rockets 4 LOS ANGELES, CA – APRIL 21: Kevin Durant #7 of the Houston Rockets looks on during the game against the Los Angeles Lakers on April 21, 2026 at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Juan Ocampo/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images Houston is a team the Suns don’t match up well against. They have athletic defenders on the perimeter, size inside, and elite scorers that can close out games in the clutch. The Suns struggled in their regular season matchups against the Rockets last season, losing all four. The Rockets are in a similar position to the Suns, where they are leaning on a second year of continuity and improved injury luck to improve off last season’s disappointing finish. While I don’t think Houston is necessarily better than teams that I’ll discuss as possible series wins for the Suns, I do think they are one of the worst postseason matchups the Suns could face. Suns 4 – Nuggets 3 Nikola Jokic has done his time with the Nuggets, and it shows. By this time next year or the year after, he will be teaming up with Luka on the Lakers and the Nuggets will sink back into the depths of the Western Conference. Until then, I think the Suns, like every team in the league, will have their hands full with Jokic. This year with Maluach and possibly a healthy Mark Williams, the Suns will have the length and strength to at least make things difficult for the two-time MVP. Denver is, at the end of the day, a finesse team, and the Suns’ new physical defense could give Denver’s potent offense problems they haven’t been able to give them in past matchups. Still, I think the Suns will need to run the total up when Jokic hits the bench, and the role players will have to deliver an outsized performance for that to happen. Add to that the altitude, and this is a series that screams out for the Suns to secure a 3-4 seed if they want to advance against the Nuggets. Suns 4 – Lakers 3 The Lakers are retooling for life after Bron, but by the time the playoffs roll around, they should have most of the kinks worked out. There are questions about the defensive acumen of the Lakers’ starting guards, and the Booker/Green backcourt may prove too much for even the best defensive efforts of Luka and Reeves. Answers to Luka Doncic on offense are hard to come by, and as the Suns saw in ‘22, home-court advantage doesn’t guarantee anything, but if the Suns sneak into a 5 or 6 seed, I like their chances against the Lakers better than a potential matchup against the Rockets or Nuggets. Suns 4 – Timberwolves 1 Close your eyes and repeat after me. Suns first-round matchup against the Timberwolves. Now say this seven times in the mirror every morning until the playoffs start. This is the clearest path to backing up Ishbia’s bold claim. They moved off of the size that made Minnesota a difficult matchup in hopes of Lamelo being something he hasn’t proven to be in the NBA: a winner. If the Timberwolves make it through the regular season without completely unraveling, the Suns will mop them up in the first round. There are still a lot of questions to be answered about who each of these teams are going to be by the time the playoffs roll around. There may be some young upstart teams, such as the Jazz or Trail Blazers, that sneak into the top 6. But it seems to me significant that Ishbia and the Suns organization feel optimistic internally. He didn’t set any expectations for the 45-win Suns team to win a playoff series last season. Mat Ishbia is always confident, but never full of expletive. If he says it will happen. I give it a 60 percent chance that it will. That’s a number. To me, it all depends on who we play, but others might think differently. Let me know in the chat what teams you think give the Suns the best chance to advance, or which teams you think the Suns need to avoid at all costs.

stories.title: Miles McBride’s agent leaves door open for future talks with Knicks
stories.summary: Of the three Knicks who did not get a contract extension heading into the season, Miles McBride’s long-term future with the team is the most at risk.
stories.detailText: Miles McBride claps his hands during the Knicks' preseason win over the Raptors on Oct. 15, 2026 at Madison Square Garden. Of the three Knicks who did not get their desired contract extension heading into the season, Miles McBride’s long-term future with the team is the most at risk . His agent, Mark Bartelstein, opened up about the team shutting down all extension negotiations . “No doubt, he would love to get that,” Bartelstein said on SiriusXM NBA Radio. “But at the end of the day, you work for the Knicks and it takes two sides to get a deal done. And if the Knicks aren’t ready to do extensions right now, then we just gotta buckle up and go have a great season. He’ll be a free agent this summer, but we’ll see. We’ve got a great relationship with [president] Leon [Rose] and the front office. We’ll see: there may be opportunities during the season, maybe in the near future. Who knows where we’ll be able to have those conversations.” McBride is set to make just under $4 million in the final year of his contract this season and will be in line for a dramatic raise if he hits free agency next summer. Miles McBride claps his hands during the Knicks’ preseason win over the Raptors on Oct. 15, 2026 at Madison Square Garden. Jason Szenes for New York Post Operating under owner James Dolan’s demand to stay under the second apron, it will be extremely difficult for the Knicks to have all five starters on big contracts and still have space left over to give a significant contract to a bench player. That makes McBride the most likely trade candidate on the roster before the Knicks potentially lose him for nothing in the summer. And he is someone, as a proven bench contributor currently on a cheap deal, who would actually bring back a strong return. The Post’s Stefan Bondy predicted in his season preview that McBride will be moved. McBride has not been as pointed as Karl-Anthony Towns about the negotiations, but he did make it clear that he felt he deserved an extension before the Knicks shut down talks. “We’ve spoken to the Knicks throughout the summer,” Bartelstein said. “Miles, like any player in his position, would love to get an extension. I think he’s earned it. He’s been a huge part of where that organization has gone over the last three or four years. He’s been their sixth man. A lot of people don’t realize how hurt he played last year in the playoffs. He had abdominal surgery that caused him to miss a couple of months. He came back and he wasn’t really right yet, but he didn’t want to miss the opportunity to be there for his teammates.” Dink Pate’s wild basketball journey has landed him back with the Knicks. The team signed him to an Exhibit 10 contract Saturday and quickly waived him — a housekeeping procedure to get him to their G-League team. Since Exhibit 10 deals are basically just training camp deals, they expire at the start of the regular season. But as long as he clears waivers as expected, it means the Knicks will keep his G League rights. Pate, 20, spent last year with the Westchester Knicks. Then, as part of college sports’ increasingly Wild West-like system, he tried to play in college this year at Providence. He didn’t have previous college experience, having instead opted to play for the G League Ignite before entering the draft last year, where he went undrafted and signed with the Knicks. But the NCAA recently denied Pate’s amateur status and ruled him ineligible. So with his college hopes dashed, he’s likely headed back to the G League. Pate, a 6-foot-8 guard, averaged 16.0 points and 3.7 assists with the Westchester Knicks during the G League regular season last year. Joel Embiid isn’t planning on taking in the Knicks’ championship festivities before their season opener Tuesday night against the 76ers and Madison Square Garden. “I don’t really feel like watching that whole ceremony,” Embiid said. “I guess I’ll be in the locker room.” Jaylen Brown, though, had a different sentiment. “It’s an honor,” Brown said. “Opening night, it’s primetime, the former champions, I think it’s serendipitous.”

stories.title: Mavs’ roster moves: Cooper Flagg and John Poulakidas news
stories.summary: The Mavericks fine-tuned their roster just days before the season tips off
stories.detailText: MACAU, CHINA - OCTOBER 11: Cooper Flagg of Dallas Mavericks during the NBA China Games 2026 between the Dallas Mavericks and Houston Rockets at The Venetian Arena on the Cotai Strip on October 11, 2026 in Macau, China. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Clicks Images/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Dallas Mavericks wrapped up their preseason schedule with a loss to the Atlanta Hawks Friday night . Despite a relatively mundane record (1-3), the preseason allowed Kyrie Irving a chance to prove he’s returning to form and showed how Zaccharie Risacher can contribute when he’s playing at his best (which in fairness, took until the final game). With the preseason behind them and the regular season just days away, Dallas continues to handle some roster business. This is the time of year when moves around the edges are made and players on the cusp are either retained or let free. In the case of the Mavericks, they made two moves involving familiar names – one, the face of the franchise and the other a rotation piece at the end of last season. John Poulakidas The Mavericks gave Poulakidas a two-way contract on March 2, 2026. This was after Dallas traded Anthony Davis and unequivocally ushed in the Cooper Flagg era. With Dallas’ season effectively over by early March, it made sense to take a few flyers and Poulakidas was one of them. For a team that shot below league average from beyond the arc, Poulakidas was a welcome sight and seemingly would have a chance on a Mavs’ team that struggled from deep. In 13 games with the Mavericks, Poulakidas averaged just shy of 20 minutes per game, and offered up 8.8 points and 2.3 assists per game across those outings. He was everything the team needed as a shooter, having connected on 57.1% of his shots inside the arc and 40.3% from deep. Despite that, Poulakidas’ time as a Maverick has come to an end as of Saturday afternoon. As part of their effort to get to the proper number of roster spots, Poulakidas was waived. If you’re wondering whether or not this move was in direct correlation to keeping Dwight Powell, it seems to be only part of the story. Even with the departure of Poulakidas, Dallas has to eliminate another standard contract to be in compliance with the 15-man maximum, which means Powell himself could be dropped, is someone else isn’t moved out in order to retain him. Cooper Flagg In the least surprising news of the offseason, the Mavericks opted to pick up Flagg’s third year option. A player like Flagg – one who signed their rookie deal last year and who hold a year of NBA tenure – puts his team in position to pick up (or not) their third-year option. This is generally a no-brainer for most teams, given the relative affordability of a rookie-scale deal, but it was of course the most elementary thing imaginable for a player of Flagg’s caliber. The move locks in Flagg for 2027-2028 at just north of $15 million. Next year, Dallas will all but certainly do it all again, to lock Flagg in for 2028-2029. Adjacent to this news is the curious lack of similar news for Risacher. He too is in position to either get his next year locked up, or not . Having started all four preseason games doesn’t necessarily indicate what will happen. On the surface, his starts suggest he will be a big part of the rotation, possibly even a day-one starter. Perhaps it was more of an effort to give him the necessary burn for the Mavericks front office to make the most informed decision. Dallas still has time to announce his news, so it’s not time to read into anything, but it is something to monitor as we near the November 2 deadline to lock him in. I invite you to follow me @_80MPH on X, and check back often at Mavs Moneyball for all the latest on the Dallas Mavericks.

stories.title: Kevin Durant has another social media beef, this time with Suns owner Mat Ishbia, Dillon Brooks
stories.summary: Ishbia joins the illustrious club of Klay Thompson, Kendrick Perkins, and others who have gotten into a social media tiff with Durant.
stories.detailText: Kevin Durant has never shied away from social media beefs. The Houston Rockets forward's latest target for internet clapbacks is Phoenix Suns owner Mat Ishbia. Durant played for the Suns from 2023 to 2025 and still seems to have some feelings. Ishbia gave an interview on CNBC Sports' podcast and brought up Phoenix's 2023 acquisition of Durant. The quote that X account Fullcourtpass pulled out from the interview was "I kind of threw money at the problem… Bringing in super talented players like Kevin Durant doesn't necessarily lead to championships." Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Basketball league for the 2026-27 NBA season Durant then quoted this post and said, "#blameKD even though KD stayed on top of his game at 36 and got u back this "culture" you love so much. Aye, Matthew acts like I got arrested for a DUI or sumn. Back to threads." By this point, Durant had played 36 games in the 2024-25 season. He averaged 26.6 points, 6.0 rebounds and 4.2 assists per game. His average points per game was his second-highest over his last four seasons. This drew a response from Ishbia , who said, "You obviously didn't watch the clip. Didn't blame you @kdtrey5, but am happy with the culture we are building here in Phoenix. We got the right guys and right focus now and are excited for this season. Good luck this season in Houston." Durant responded directly to Ishbia. "U should be giving Thanks every chance u get. You don't have to pay me an absurd amount of money to play for another team." Later, current Suns forwad Dillon Brooks posted on his Instagram story, subtweeting Durant’s X interaction. Dillon Brooks responds to Kevin Durant 🍿 “Thanks Matt for cleaning up that stench in the locker room before I came #Culture ” (h/t @CGBBURNER ) https://t.co/7JnNpqxA9O pic.twitter.com/OVfiKsYN4W — Fullcourtpass (@Fullcourtpass) October 18, 2026 The veteran forward was traded to Phoenix at the 2023 NBA trade deadline in a deal that included five total players and five picks. He was then traded to the Rockets ahead of the 2025-26 regular season in a seven-team deal. Brooks landed with the Suns as part of the same deal. Houston and Phoenix will play three times this season, first on Nov. 7, and then again on Nov. 25. The Rockets and Suns will meet again Feb. 5 for the series finale.

stories.title: Knicks waive Bruce Brown, keep James Wiseman ahead of opener
stories.summary: The Knicks are waiving Bruce Brown and keeping James Wiseman on the roster as the team heads into its regular-season opener, sources told ESPN.
stories.detailText: The New York Knicks waived Bruce Brown and will keep James Wiseman on the roster as the team heads into its regular-season opener. Brown was one of several players on non-guaranteed deals vying for one of New York's final two available roster spots. Tony Bradley , Ochai Agbaji and Drew Eubanks also were waived in recent days. Wiseman appeared in all four of the Knicks' preseason games and impressed in 24 minutes versus the Toronto Raptors on Tuesday, when he scored 18 points and grabbed 10 rebounds. According to ESPN's Bobby Marks, the Knicks could have kept Brown and Wiseman , but because they are only $3.2 million below their self-imposed hard cap at the second apron, retaining both players would've been difficult. Wiseman, 25, will join Karl-Anthony Towns and Andre Drummond in New York's center rotation. The reigning NBA champions lost key reserve big man Mitchell Robinson to the Boston Celtics this past summer via free agency. The Knicks will begin the NBA's regular season Tuesday when they host the new-look Philadelphia 76ers .

teamStories.detailText: SAN ANTONIO, TX - OCTOBER 14: Victor Wembanyama #1 of the San Antonio Spurs smiles before the game against the Phoenix Suns on October 14, 2026 at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photos by Michael Gonzales/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images Every year there’s an abundance of lists that come out about the NBA’s players, coaches and teams, and none matter more than the general manager survey released before the season. The latest one was published on Thursday, and according to most top executives, Victor Wembanyama is primed to have one of the greatest seasons of all time in 2026-27. He got the most votes to win Defensive player of the Year as well the majority for the MVP crown, and the San Antonio Spurs are the favorite to win the title. Holy moly, such a season hasn’t been logged since the great Hakeem Olajuwon in 1993-94. Keep in mind that the NBA’s DPOY award started in the 1982-83 season, yet even if it existed earlier, the only bigs who could have arguably won it, earned the MVP and led a team to the chip were Bill Russell, Wilt Chamberlain and Kareem Abdul-Jabbar. Yet don’t forget that Michael Jordan claimed both awards in 1987-88, but his team lost in the Eastern Conference Finals. LeBron James would have been the first to accomplish this feat since Olajuwon, but he got robbed of the DPOY in 2012-13. Olajuwon, who played three years at school and didn’t simultaneously win both awards until he was 31, was already on a tear when he turned 23. That was in his second season and at that age had already ascended into one of the most devastating players in NBA history. He was skinnier then, but an athletic marvel who could down turnaround jumpers with ease and soar through the lane. He wanted the big moment, and in Mirin Fader’s biography about him, there is a great line where he defended himself against complaining teammates for taking a shot with multiple defenders on him because he was the one paid to take that shot. Wembanyama is only entering his fourth season and will turn 23 on Jan. 4. He has gotten closer to his grown man body every year and like the young Olajuwon, needs to be defended with all five players plus is a factor in fourth quarters, as he averaged 6.3 points in those periods during the playoffs. At this point, the only heavyweight on his level is Nikola Jokić, yet most GMs picked him over Wemby as the best center. That won’t be for long if he keeps improving at rapid speed and one example of how he has is the speed and timing of his pick-and-roll defense from his rookie year in 2023-24 until now. He impacts the game in more ways, so when his playmaking catches up to the Joker, he’ll jump to his own tier. He may never turn into the wow-passer Jokić is, but Wembanyama has the talent to average a triple-double, too. In 2026-27, the race for the MVP should come down to Wemby, Luka Dončić, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Giannis Antetokounmpo and Jokić, assuming they stay healthy, because they have a chance to win enough and put up incredible numbers. Wemby being the best in the league at guarding two players at once and creating a big intimidation factor with his shot blocking, will give him an edge over the field, while double-dipping for the other award. Notably, only three of the last 10 GM polls have correctly predicted who would win the MVP award. Three of the last 10 polls also predicted the correct champion, but two of those were very easy to call since they were the Kevin Durant and Stephen Curry-led Golden State Warriors. Still, lots of those teams that were picked to win and didn’t were not as deep as the current Spurs. Don’t be surprised if Dylan Harper, who most GMs picked to have a breakout season, produces like an All-Star off the bench because he was already a major player to end last postseason. Next season, the Spurs will have a target on their backs, but it won’t matter much because they have good coaching and a surplus of motivated talent spearheaded by Wemby. Most GMs don’t always get it right, but they believe he’s going to take over the league like only the most special have, so maybe opposing teams should take the survey as a bad omen.

teamStories.summary: Hopes for the San Antonio Spurs are high, unlike those of the Dodgers and Rams.
teamStories.detailText: SAN ANTONIO, TX -SEPTEMBER 28: Stephon Castle #5, De'Aaron Fox 34 and Dylan Harper #2 of the San Antonio Spurs pose for photos during San Antonio Spurs Media Day at Victory Capital Performance Center on September 28, 2026 in San Antonio, Texas. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Ronald Cortes/Getty Images) | Getty Images At the start of October, I had high hopes for a fan’s Triple Crown for 2026-27. My main team, the Spurs, are co-favorites to win it all this season. My two local teams were also favorites – the Dodgers were already into the NLCS looking for a three-peat, and the Rams were everyone’s favorite to win the Super Bowl. While nothing has changed for the Spurs, a lot has changed for the Dodgers and Rams. The Dodgers, two-time defending World Series champs, were just swept 4 – 0 by the Milwaukee Brewers. Preseason favorite Rams are 2 – 3, and about to fall three games behind the 49ers, who are now Vegas favorites. At least the Rams have better chances than the Dodgers, who have none. To make it worse, I just realized that if we look backwards, each of my teams lost in the “final four” for each of their leagues. The Rams lost to the Seahawks in the NFC Championship game, the Spurs in the NBA Finals, and the Dodgers lost to the Brewers. Just like the Spurs against the Knicks, the Dodgers led in every game. I don’t know what you would call the opposite of my hoped-for Triple Crown, but it would not be very nice. But let’s look forward instead of back. The Spurs remain co-favorites with OKC to win it all this season. Indeed, league GMs picked the Spurs ahead of OKC to prevail, with 77% predicting that Victor Wembayama will be the MVP. 2,000% of the GMs also predicted that Victor would repeat as Defensive Player of the Year, though I might have that percentage slightly off. Closer to the main point of this post, Dylan Harper was voted the player most likely to have a break-out year, ahead of Cooper Flagg (27% to 7%). That vote may reflect that Flagg is starting at a much higher baseline, as he averaged 21 points, 6.7 boards and 4.5 assists last season. It is a bit harder to “break out” from numbers like that. But I do want to address the “three guard” debate going on in the Spurs universe. I addressed this point several times last season, pointing out that having three excellent guards is a good thing and not a “problem”. For instance, even before training camp opened in 2025, I wrote this: “The basketball universe unanimously approved the Spurs’ selection on Dylan Harper as the clear second best player in the 2025 NBA draft. The only concern I have heard is that Harper’s skills overlap with those of the anticipated starting backcourt of De’Aaron Fox and Stephon Castle. Having coached a bit, I know that having three good guards for the two backcourt spots is a good thing, not a bad one. The reason is simple — players don’t play all 48 minutes. Indeed, the Spurs’ best player last year (you know his name) averaged just 33 minutes per game. In 17 games with the Spurs, Fox averaged 34 minutes while Castle averaged 27. If Fox and Castle play the same amount this season, they will play a total of 61 minutes out of the 96 minutes available. That leaves 35 minutes for Harper or others — for instance. if Devin Vassell splits his time between the 2 and the 3. Harper will be not be 20 years old until March 2026 — and 20 is probably about the right number of minutes for such a young player in his rookie season.” This prediction was remarkably accurate – in the regular season, Fox averaged 31 minutes, Castle 30 and Harper 22. In the playoffs, those numbers ticked up to 33, 33 and 27. Interestingly, Devin Vassel led the team in playoff minutes with 34.8 per game, slightly more than Victor. Of course, Victor was ejected early in a T’Wolves game, pushing his average minutes per game down a bit. But back to the three guards issue. Fox, Castle and Harper’s playoff minutes totaled 93 minutes per game, very close to the 96 minutes available for the two guard spots. Which meant that the Spurs had two of their excellent guards on the floor virtually all the time – just the way you want it. If the Spurs play all three of them at the same time for portions of each game, and try to keep the per player minutes close to 32 per game, that will necessarily mean that for portions of each game, only one of them will be on the floor. If the goal is to maximize the number of lead ball-handlers on the floor, last season’s system seems preferable. (Side note – the Spurs won 62 games last season and made it to the NBA Finals. If it ain’t broke, don’t fix it.). I am certainly OK with increasing Harper’s minutes from the 22 he played in the regular season, and the 27 in the playoffs, but that can be done with the 2026-27 season model instead of forcing a three guard line-up. Indeed, no one on the Spurs averaged more than 32 minutes per game in the regular season – a Spurs tradition that keeps the players fresh and their careers long. This also allows the non-starters to get real minutes and stay sharp. So long as Harper is getting his minutes, no one should care who is starting. Something Manu Ginobili can certainly attest to. This is especially true because while the Spurs do not have a logjam at guard, they do in the frontcourt. Assuming Victor, Luke Kornet and the rookie soak up all 48 of the center minutes, that leaves 96 minutes for the two frontcourt spots. And the Spurs have a bunch of good players vying for those minutes. Vassel, Julian Champagnie, Tobias Harris, Keldon Johnson, Carter Bryant, and Harrison Barnes. That is six legitimate NBA players. Last season, the two starters, Vassel and Champaigne, combined for 58 of the 96 minutes. Harris averaged 28 minutes in Detroit, and should play about the same this year. We are up to 86 minutes, leaving only 10 minutes for 6 th Man of the Year Johnson, potential star Bryant and whatever minutes Barnes gets. If the Spurs use the three guard line-up for even ten minutes per game, that leaves ZERO minutes for Johnson, Bryant and Barnes. And I am pretty sure the Spurs don’t want to significantly cut the minutes of either Vassel or Champagnie. Fun fact: those two had the second and third best plus-minus on the team. You can guess who had the best. If I had a vote, which I don’t, I would vote for minimizing the three-guard line-up. POSTSCRIPT: I wrote most of this before the Spurs’ Friday night preseason game against the Kings. The Spurs started the game with the three-guard line-up, plus Vassel and Victor. When the Spurs made their first substitution (Champagnie for Fox) at the 6:34 mark of the first quarter, they were already up by 16 points, 24 – 8. Mitch Johnson said that they will start the three guards against OKC in the season opener on Tuesday. Maybe that is why I don’t have a vote.

teamStories.summary: The Spurs have their roster locked in, and there are no big surprises.
teamStories.detailText: SAN ANTONIO, TX - OCTOBER 16: Victor Wembanyama #1 of the San Antonio Spurs looks on during the game against the Sacramento Kings during a 2026 NBA Preseason game on October 16, 2026 at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photos by Michael Gonzales/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images The Spurs’ roster is set for opening night, the team announced. There are no big surprises. As expected, San Antonio will carry 14 standard contracts into the regular season, with those going to De’Aaron Fox, Jordan McLaughlin, Stephon Castle, Dylan Harper, Devin Vassell, Julian Champagnie, Keldon Johnson, Carter Bryant, Harrison Barnes, Tobias Harris, Jayden Quaintance, Tarris Reed Jr., Luke Kornet, and Victor Wembanyama. The three two-way deals will go to the returning David Jones-Garcia and 2026 Draft second-rounders Maliq Brown and Ja’Kobi Gillespie. The decision to leave one standard roster spot open is likely tied to the franchise’s cap situation. The Spurs could have only signed a player with no NBA experience to a minimum contract if they wanted to avoid the luxury tax line. Anyone with experience would have pushed them over it. With so much depth and youth already in place, it made sense to keep the slot available in case of a trade or signing opportunity during the season. Similarly, there was not a lot of suspense about the two-way deals. The Spurs selected Gillespie and Brown with the 42nd and 44th overall picks in the 2026 NBA Draft, so they clearly were enticed by their talent. Jones-Garcia was a standout during Summer League last year, and while he suffered a season-ending injury last season and didn’t shine in preseason, the soon-to-be 25-year-old scorer could become a contributor at the NBA level. It’s not easy to come up with a depth chart for this year’s iteration, in part because they are set to start three lead guards and a wing at power forward, but there’s clearly enough depth at every position to think another successful season is ahead. Expectations are high, as the Spurs won 62 regular-season games and reached the NBA Finals last year, but the talent for another deep run is clearly in place. The Spurs will start their season by hosting last year’s Conference Finals opponent, the Oklahoma City Thunder, on Oct. 20th. Tip-off is scheduled for 8:30 p.m. CT.

stories.summary: — Drake Maye threw three touchdown passes, New England overcame losing three offensive linemen and Charles Woods came up with Geno Smith's first interception of the season in the fourth quarter to help the Patriots hold on for a 26-19 win over the New...
stories.detailText: FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- — Drake Maye threw three touchdown passes, New England overcame losing three offensive linemen and Charles Woods came up with Geno Smith 's first interception of the season in the fourth quarter to help the Patriots hold on for a 26-19 win over the New York Jets on Sunday. Maye completed 18 of 32 passes for 235 yards in his third consecutive game with at least three TD passes. Romeo Doubs , DeMario Douglas and Hunter Henry had touchdown catches for the Patriots (4-2), who have won three in a row. Douglas had a team-high seven catches for 86 yards. A.J. Brown had three catches for 27 yards for the Patriots in his return from injured reserve, but his timing was off and had three drops on his 10 total targets. New England won its fourth straight against the Jets and 19th in its last 21 meetings despite right tackle Morgan Moses (ankle), left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) and right guard Ben Brown (knee) leaving with injuries. The Jets (2-4) had a chance to tie it in the third quarter, but the Patriots held them to a field goal. New York squandered another opportunity to cut the deficit to a field goal in the fourth quarter when Smith was picked off by Woods. It came on Smith's 166th pass of the season, ending his longest opening stretch to a season without an interception. Smith finished 20 of 30 for 252 yards a touchdown to rookie Omar Cooper Jr ., who had six catches for 103 yards in his return from IR after missing four games with an ankle injury. New England's defense, which got a boost from cornerback Christian Gonzalez returning from a two-game absence with a shoulder injury, held New York to 0 for 3 in the red zone. The Jets were also 3 of 10 on third down and were stopped on fourth-down runs on consecutive possessions in the second quarter. The Patriots led 17-3 at the half, courtesy of Doubs’ diving 42-yard touchdown catch and a 9-yard scoring grab by Douglas. The Jets trimmed the gap to 17-10 in the third quarter after Cooper got behind Patriots safety Craig Woodson and caught a 42-yard TD from Smith. That remained the score when Jets edge rusher David Bailey stripped TreVeyon Henderson of the ball and Jamien Sherwood recoverer at the New England 36. New York drove to 10, but Smith was sacked by Elijah Ponder , forcing the Jets to settle for a 36-yard field goal by Jason Sanders . The Patriots responded on their next series, capping a 12-play, 68-yard drive with a 7-yard TD strike from Maye to Henry, but Andy Borregales missed the extra point. Just four plays later and the Jets down 10, Smith overshot Kenyon Sadiq on a deep pass that was intercepted by Woods. Injuries Jets: LB Kiko Mauigoa left with a thigh injury in the first quarter. Patriots: Doubs (shoulder) exited in the first quarter following his touchdown catch and didn’t return. ... Moses favored his left ankle when he left early in the second quarter. ... Vera-Tucker left in the second with a hamstring injury and was ruled out. ... Brown had trouble putting weight on his left leg as he was helped off in the fourth quarter with a knee injury. Up next Jets: Host the Dolphins next Sunday. Patriots: Visit the Bears on Thursday night. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here

stories.title: Falcons' Kendal Daniels hurts neck on tackle vs. Bears, hospitalized
stories.summary: Kendal Daniels is alert and has movement in all his extremities, the Falcons said Sunday, after he injured his neck on a tackle attempt vs. the Bears.
stories.detailText: ATLANTA -- Kendal Daniels is alert and has movement in all his extremities, the Falcons said Sunday, after the rookie linebacker was carted off the field with a neck injury suffered on an ugly-looking collision during the team's 31-23 loss to the Chicago Bears . With the Bears leading 21-7 with 8:48 left in the third quarter, Daniels dived in to tackle Colston Loveland after a Caleb Williams pass completion and the linebacker's head appeared to collide with the tight end's left leg near the knee. Daniels remained down on the field for some time as medical personnel tended to him. They stabilized his neck and body, then loaded him onto the cart in a gurney as Falcons players and coaches gathered around and wished him well. On the way off the field, Daniels made a fist with his left hand. "He said, 'Y'all go finish this off.' He was in good spirits," quarterback Michael Penix Jr . said. The team said Daniels was taken to Grady Memorial Hospital for further evaluation. "Those are no fun for anybody," coach Kevin Stefanski said. "Players, coaches. You don't want to see anyone down like that. Kendal is a kid we all love, we all respect. "All the reports are good, and we're praying that they remain good." Daniels, a fourth-round draft pick out of Oklahoma, has been a starter since Week 1. He was wearing the green dot as the defensive playcaller at the time of the injury with Divine Deablo out with an arm injury. Linebacker Josh Woods took over the green dot with Daniels out.

stories.title: Tracking Jaguars CB/WR Travis Hunter's 2026 season: A career best in Week 6?
stories.summary: Every week, we will look at how many snaps the two-way corner/receiver plays on offense and defense. Is there a trend in his usage?
stories.detailText: The Jacksonville Jaguars were emphatic in the offseason that cornerback/wide receiver Travis Hunter was going to play on both sides of the ball in 2026. However, unlike his rookie season, the plan was for the 2025 No. 2 overall pick to be a starter on defense. Now, he is just being mixed in on offense with a specific package of plays. The situation is fluid, though, and head coach Liam Coen has maintained that Hunter's usage could change weekly. "You want to continue to do what we think is going to give us the best chance at winning throughout the course of the week," he said. "And so, if that's Travis getting more touches [on offense], then [he] absolutely will." Hunter played more on offense than defense in his 2025 rookie season, which ended after seven games because of a right knee injury. The 2024 Heisman Trophy winner had 28 catches for 298 yards and a touchdown and 15 tackles and three pass breakups. He played 67% of the team's offensive snaps and 36% of the defensive snaps before his injury, which occurred during practice on Oct. 30. How has Hunter's usage evolved this season? Each week we'll track his stats and evaluate the impact he had on the game. Week 6 vs. Houston Texans in London Hunter had the best game of his career against the Texans at Wembley Stadium, catching four passes for 59 yards and a touchdown and also intercepting C.J. Stroud in the end zone. He's just the fourth player since the 1970 AFL/NFL merger with a receiving touchdown and interception in the same game and the first to do it since Philadelphia's Brian Dawkins in 2002. The touchdown and interception came on consecutive drives. Per NFL Next Gen Stats, Hunter had 34 coverage snaps and limited the Texans to two catches on five targets. However, he also was hit with a questionable pass interference penalty in the end zone against Nico Collins that gave the Texans the ball at the 1-yard line late in the first half. Despite that, this was the first time Hunter has made a significant impact on both sides of the ball -- 58 snaps on defense and 9 on offense (season high) -- in the same game in his 13 career games. Week 5 vs. Philadelphia Eagles in London Hunter played every defensive snap (59) for the second week in a row and had six tackles (second-most on the team) and a pass breakup. He was penalized for defensive pass interference that wiped out a third-and-17 incompletion in the second quarter. It gave the Eagles the ball at the Jaguars' 3-yard line and Philadelphia running back Will Shipley scored two plays later. On offense, Hunter played five snaps and touched the ball for the first time since Week 1, catching a 9-yard pass on second-and-7 from the Jaguars' 40-yard line. Parker Washington scored on a 51-yard catch-and-run on the next play. Week 4 at Cincinnati Bengals Hunter played every defensive snap (71) in a 22-17 win against the Bengals and had four tackles and two pass breakups. It's the first time in his career he's played every defensive snap and it was necessary because the Jaguars were down cornerbacks Montaric Brown (hamstring) and Christian Braswell (knee) because of injury. "He played his ass off today," head coach Liam Coen said. Hunter, however, called his play "decent" and was disappointed that his interception got erased by a roughing the passer penalty on defensive tackle Arik Armstead . "I like to criticize myself a lot harder," Hunter said. "My wife does, too. I still give up a catch today, so she's going to be on me about that when I get home." Hunter didn't play at all on offense, the first time in his career that has happened. Coen said he didn't want to risk him getting hurt on that side of the ball because that would leave them down three cornerbacks. Hunter said he wasn't mad at that decision. Week 3 vs. New England Patriots In a 35-6 win against the Patriots, Hunter saw an increase in snaps with 42 on defense (70%) and a decrease on offense with four snaps (6.7% of all offensive snaps). He recorded four tackles and his first career interception, picking off New England quarterback Drake Maye in the back of the end zone late in the first half to preserve the Jaguars' 14-3 lead. Maye was trying to hit receiver Efton Chism III on third-and-goal from the 2-yard line, but Hunter out-jumped Chism for the ball. Hunter didn't touch the ball on offense for the second consecutive game, leaving him with only two touches so far this season. Week 2 at Denver Broncos Hunter played 43 total snaps in the loss against the Broncos: 35 on defense (59.3% of all defensive snaps), seven on offense (12.7% of all offensive snaps) and one on special teams. He had one pass breakup and four tackles, and he was penalized for pass interference on a Bo Nix sideline pass to receiver Courtland Sutton . The 22-yard penalty -- plus Coen's unsportsmanlike conduct penalty for arguing the call -- gave the Broncos the ball at the Jaguars' 3-yard line. The Broncos scored what turned out to be the game-winning touchdown on the next play. Hunter was not targeted on offense. After Week 2, Coen explained that his cornerbacks are handling drives with a planned rotation -- which is why Hunter was in for only 59.3% of defensive plays. "We did it for the most part of the last season as well, before Travis got hurt," Coen said. "It's something that we got to continue to do. We have corners that we have confidence in. Those guys can all make plays for us. They can all communicate for us. They've been in the system now. "But yeah, it's a rotation. Pre-game, we have it all laid out. The players know it. They all know the rotation. It's been clearly laid out to them what the expectations and standards are." Week 1 vs. Cleveland Browns Hunter started at cornerback and played 27 snaps on defense (55.1% of total defensive snaps) and four on offense (7.1% of total offensive snaps) against the Browns. On offense, he had one carry for 3 yards on a jet sweep and one catch for 8 yards on a screen pass. He has had at least one catch in every game in which he played (eight games) to this point. On defense, Hunter was targeted once on defense which resulted in a Deshaun Watson completed a 4-yard pass to KC Concepcion .

stories.title: NFL: Steelers-Saints in Paris still on despite civil unrest, protests in France
stories.summary: The Week 7 game between the New Orleans Saints and Pittsburgh Steelers on Oct. 25 in Paris is still scheduled as planned despite civil unrest and protests in France, the NFL said.
stories.detailText: The Week 7 game between the New Orleans Saints and Pittsburgh Steelers on Oct. 25 in Paris is still scheduled as planned despite civil unrest and protests in France. "Preparations continue as scheduled for NFL events and the game at Stade de France next Sunday," the NFL said in a statement. "We continue to work closely with local authorities and partners on all operational and security matters. We are also providing the two clubs with regular updates. There's been no disruption or impact at league sites." The Saints are planning to travel to Paris immediately after their game against the New York Giants in East Rutherford, New Jersey, on Sunday. The Steelers plan to practice in Pittsburgh before departing for France on Thursday. The game -- the first ever to be played in France -- will be held north of Paris at Stade de France. Saints spokesman Greg Bensel said the team concurs with the NFL's statement and is planning to play. "In addition to working closely with the NFL, we have also maintained daily security updates with our security partners in France," Bensel said. "Members of our football operations staff and internal security team have been on the ground in France for the past few days and there has been no disruption or impact at any of our team sites." Police arrested at least 1,800 people across France after violent groups clashed with officers and looted shops during nationwide demonstrations that drew hundreds of thousands protesting rising living costs and poor conditions in schools. Masked groups set fires and attacked public buildings, including city halls, in several cities on Saturday, authorities said. President Emmanuel Macron was scheduled to hold an emergency meeting with senior government officials Sunday before addressing the nation at 8 p.m. local time, his office said. The Associated Press contributed to this report.

stories.detailText: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - OCTOBER 18: Jeffery Simmons #98 of the Tennessee Titans celebrates after sacking Daniel Jones #17 of the Indianapolis Colts during the fourth quarter of the game at Lucas Oil Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tennessee Titans improved to 1-5 with their 26-20 win over the Indianapolis Colts. They were down 13-0 at the half, but scored 20 unanswered points to start the second half. Special teams played a huge role in the win. They returned a blocked punt for a touchdown and Chimere Dike had a huge 58-yard punt return that set up Carnell Tate’s first career touchdown catch. Cam Ward struggled in the win with just 102 yards passing. Hr threw one touchdown and one interception. The Titans are going to need more from him going forward, but this week should go a little easier for him with the Titans getting the win. This was Robert Saleh’s first win as the coach of the Titans. His defense had an outstanding day. They forced 3 turnovers. Daniel Jones was picked off twice, and Jeffery Simmons forced and recovered a Jonathan Taylor fumble on the Colts’ first possession of the second half. That was the play that really changed the momentum in the game. This team still feels like it has more questions than answers, but it will be a good week inside that building. Hopefully, they can build off of this one.

stories.title: Chargers WR Ladd McConkey evaluated for concussion vs. Chiefs
stories.summary: Ladd McConkey remains injured for the Los Angeles Chargers.
stories.detailText: Los Angeles Chargers wide receiver Ladd McConkey is being evaluated by the medical staff after suffering a head injury in the first half of the team’s Week 6 game against the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium. During the broadcast, it was announced that McConkey would be out for the remainder of the game. So far this season, McConkey has 12 catches for 183 yards and a touchdown as he has been dealing with a foot injury that put him on the injury report during the week. He was limited in the first two practices of the week but was a full participant on Friday and active for the game. Unfortunately, it appears the injury bug has stung him once again. McConkey’s foot injury caused him to leave the game early in Week 4 against the Seattle Seahawks, and he did not play in the team’s loss last week against the Denver Broncos. With McConkey getting evaluated for a concussion and Tre’ Harris out due to a hamstring injury, the team will rely on Quentin Johnston and KeAndre Lambert-Smith as its top receivers. Other players will need to step up across the offense in order for the team to try and win their first game of the season against the undefeated Chiefs. Otherwise, the Chargers could move to 0-6 on the season. The Chargers trail 9-3 against the Chiefs in the middle of the second quarter. Fans can watch the game on CBS or stream it on the Paramount Plus app.

stories.title: Week 6 Game Recap: Buccaneers blow huge lead and fall in overtime, when is enough enough?
stories.summary: Bucs vs Steelers week six game recap.
stories.detailText: TAMPA, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 18: Jalen Ramsey #5 of the Pittsburgh Steelers sacks Jalon Daniels #10 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the first half of the game at Raymond James Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images First Quarter: With a new, freshly minted victory under their belts, Tez Johnson touched the ball first for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Run, run, sack, punt— Pittsburgh ball. Run, run, incomplete pass, punt— Bucs’ ball. Fans would see another Bucs’ punt before finally jumping out their seats when Rueben Bain Jr., tipped an Aaron Rodgers pass which bounced into the hands of A’Shawn Robinson for his team-leading second interception of the season. The Bucs’ offense would convert Rueben Bain Jr.’s first impact play as a Buc into points with a Chase McLaughlin field goal. Chase’s kick, blocked at the line, still had enough oomph to scoot across the crossbar for Tampa’s first lead of the game. 3-0, Bucs. Trailing by three, the Steelers’ special team struck a big blow against their former coordinator, a kick return that made it was across midfield and into the lap of Chase McLaughlin before finally being shut down by hustling Tampa defenders. That same special teams unit un-struck their big blow, as the big return was flagged and brought back— Illegal blindside block Cole Holcomb. Aaron Rodgers and co. did earn those surrendered yards back, but their drive would ultimately lead to a Mike McCarthy decision— A fourth down with three yards to go. Despite completing a pass beyond the sticks, the Steelers lost the necessary yardage when Germie Bernard reversed course, try to double back across the field, and got tackled behind the line to gain for a crushing turnover on downs. Second Quarter: Tampa Bay’s ensuing drive featured a first for the 2026 Buccaneers and Jalon Daniels— Up tempo. The Buccaneers not only trusted their rookie passer to call the offense at the line, they trusted him to pass . Daniels, without the consistent aid of a Bucky Irving first down, run took his team down the field with passes to Chris Godwin and Emeka Egbuka— Ted Hurst III even found reps as the rookie collected a chain-moving reception, but it was also a down field pass to Hurst III that drew a pass interference and placed the ball on the Pittsburgh one-yard line. Wasting no time, Daniels dropped back and tossed his first touchdown of the day— Emeka Egbuka’s first since week two. 10-0, Buccaneers. With under five minutes remaining in half, the Jalon Daniels-Emeka Egbuka connection had a chance at their second score of the day— The duo missed. Emeka Egbuka, running wide open was slightly overthrown, forcing an attempt at a one-handed snag. The incomplete pass would lead the Bucs to Chase McLaughlin and three points. 13-0, Tampa Bay. Aaron Rodgers would be introduced to a couple of Bucs’ rookies on the next drive. Up first, Keonte Scott a slot blitz Rodgers never saw and a sack. The third down that would follow would be another introduction and a moment that many Buccaneers’ fans have been waiting for a Rueben Bain Jr. sack, the first of his career. Bain Jr.’s first career sack comes on third down against future Hall of Famer Aaron Rodgers. Congratulations To Bain Jr. and the Bucs’ defense for a near flawless performance in the first half of Sunday’s matchup. The lone flaw came in the half’s final drive. Needing points, momentum, or just a sign of life before the intermission, the Pittsburgh were able to drive into field goal range, spike the ball and give Chris Boswell the opportunity to atone for earlier miss— Miss atoned for 13-3, Buccaneers. Third Quarter: In a strange sequence, Mike McCarthy sustained an injury walking off the field and spent halftime in the blue tent so the Pittsburgh Steelers never met with their head coach during the break. Whether that was impactful or not is immeasurable, however, the Steelers looked flat as their offense debuted in the third quarter with a three and out. Their defense wasn’t necessarily around to bail them out— A 9-minute drive deep into Pittsburgh territory before Tampa had to settle for a field goal. 16-3, Buccaneers. The Steelers and Bucs would each trot out their punt teams again on the following drives, before Aaron Rodgers was back under center for the final two minutes of the third quarter. Germie Bernard’s eighth catch of the day moved Pittsburgh to the Tampa Bay 40-yard line. David Walker tried stall the attack with a sack of Aaron Rodgers, but it wasn’t enough— Third down and 16, Aaron Rodgers found DK Metcalf for 16 yards and a first down. Fourth Quarter: That conversion got the wick lit, a roughing passer penalty would follow shortly after and a brief time later the Bucs’ defense would allow their first touchdown of the game. A wide open Darnell Washington brought the Steelers within one score. 16-10, Tampa Bay. Jalon Daniels first drive of the fourth quarter was not what his team needed. Daniels, hoping his receiver could make a play, threw a ball to Emeka Egbuka in heavy coverage— Interception. Sunday’s fourth quarter saw the end of a 10-straight completion streak for Aaron Rodgers. On what was his 16th consecutive pass, Rodgers had his team in field goal position and Tampa’s turnover quickly led to points as Chris Boswell delivered. 16-13, Tampa. Back-to-back Emeka Egbuka drops handed Aaron Rodgers the ball back. DK Metcalf (and a questionable pass interference penalty) gave the Steelers another field goal and another three points. 16-16, tie. The 16-16 tie wouldn’t last long because on Tampa’s next drive Jalon Daniels looked much more like a rookie than what he has so far this season. Daniel’s found Jamel Dean— who was a Buc, but is now a Steeler— for what could and arguably should have lost Tampa Bay the game. Jamel Dean left his offense at the three yard line. Tampa Bay’s defense defended those three yards like their season was on the line. The Steelers opted for just one run play and two incomplete passes, taking no time off the clock and leaving Jalon Daniels with one shot to rally. Jalon Daniels was given an inch and he took a mile. Coming off of his one of his worst throws as a Buccaneer, Daniels responded. The rookie took his team down the field and gave his kicker (The best player on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers roster) a chance to tie. 19-19, welcome to overtime. Overtime: The Buccaneers won the toss and elected to kick. They also elected to revert back to missed tackles as the focal point of their defense. A good performance until the final 15 minutes of regulation turned horrid by end of overtime. Todd Bowles’ defense finished caving on the Steelers’ final drive of the day. Pittsburgh delivered one body shot after another to Bowles’ unit as the Bucs were backed up, backed up, and backed up further until they dam broke— Touchdown Steelers- 26-19, Pittsburgh. Jalon Daniels did give Tampa Bay a small sliver of hope before the Steelers ended Tampa’s day and possibly their season— Bucs drop 1-5.
