stories.title: Rams take 9-6 lead with Blake Corum's first receiving touchdown
stories.summary: The Rams have gotten in the end zone.
stories.detailText: The Rams have gotten in the end zone. But their kicker situation has made things more complicated than it needed to be. Blake Corum scored on a 15-yard screen that he caught and took to the paint for the first receiving touchdown of his career. That put the Rams up 9-6 over the Cardinals. But with new kicker Blake Grupe doubtful to return with a knee injury, the Rams elected to go for two. Matthew Stafford was strip-sacked on the play, and the Cardinals nearly had two points of their own when defensive lineman L.J. Collier picked up the loose ball and went running the other way. But Collier was tackled before he could get to the opposite end zone, keeping the Rams’ three-point advantage. Stafford is 9-of-13 for 60 yards with a TD.

stories.title: Instant analysis from Patriots’ 26-19 win over Jets
stories.summary: Observations from Week 6 at Gillette Stadium.
stories.detailText: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - OCTOBER 18: Charles Woods #22 of the New England Patriots celebrates with teammates after an interception against the New York Jets during the fourth quarter at Gillette Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Jaiden Tripi/Getty Images) | Getty Images A total of 45 points separated Mike Vrabel’s sideline from Aaron Glenn’s during the 2025 AFC East sweep. Enough of a gap remained Sunday at Gillette Stadium, where the New England Patriots held on to defeat the New York Jets by a score of 26-19. Here’s a glance back on the 1 p.m. ET kickoff as the head coaches move forward with 4-2 and 2-4 teams. Maye’s October rolls on After accounting for one touchdown and seven turnovers in September, the calendar has done more than flip. Drake Maye completed 18-of-32 passes for 235 yards on Sunday. The Patriots quarterback found three touchdowns and no interceptions against a much-improved Jets defense that had finished 2025 without a pick. He added 24 rushing yards over the course of the afternoon, led by a sprint of 21. Taking the field in “13” personnel, the opening drive brought a batted pass at the line of scrimmage and a three-and-out. Offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels’ group needed two plays to find paydirt on the second series, however, thanks to a clean pocket and a diving 42-yard touchdown to wide receiver Romeo Doubs. In only 12 seconds of game clock. Maye did not complete his second pass of the outing until the 6:57 mark in the second quarter, but he went 5-of-7 through the air and endured roughing the passer on the final drive going into halftime. And with a trio of timeouts on hand as well as slot receiver DeMario Douglas, a 17-3 game it became. The recent AFC Offensive Player of the Week had gone 9-of-17 for 130 yards, two touchdowns and a passer rating of 117.3 at the break. Things got out of intermission with a turnover on downs and a pair of turnovers by ground for the Patriots. But a 12-play, 63-yard surge ended in the end zone with tenured tight end Hunter Henry’s second touchdown in as many weeks. New England finished 8-of-15 on third down, 1-of-2 on fourth down and 2-of-4 in the red zone. Maye’s October now spans 10 touchdowns. Brown battles drops as wideout room brings in two touchdowns A.J. Brown had been a limited participant for three consecutive practices after having his 21-day window open. And while No. 1 was questionable to return to face the Jets, the light was left on. His official activation to the 53-man roster followed on the eve of the 1 p.m. ET kickoff. The June arrival in Foxborough was the lone wide receiver in the starting lineup on Sunday. After Brown’s first catch was overturned via challenge, it took until his fourth target to get on the board. He finished with 27 receiving yards on a team-high 10 looks in his return from the high ankle sprain that sent him to injured reserve following the season opener. Three drops, including on fourth-and-5, were in the cards along with a bobbled onside kick on the hands team. A New England wideout depth chart of four had amassed three touchdowns in the final game without its Pro Bowler. A week later, a depth chart of five brought in two scores. The aforementioned Doubs was downgraded to out due to a shoulder injury that surfaces during his latest visit to the end zone. The aforementioned Douglas tied him for the team lead with his third touchdown catch of the fall and finished Sunday with seven receptions for 86 yards. And also with a lost fumble on a 40-yard gain in the fourth quarter. Kiner paces Patriots’ backfield committee A high ankle sprain did not keep TreVeyon Henderson away from practice. The No. 38 overall pick in the 2025 NFL draft entered the weekend as questionable . He proceeded to outlast the inactives list , one loud hit from linebacker DeMario Davis and one forced fumble courtesy of defensive end David Bailey to handle 40 scrimmage yards across eight touches. Yet it was a backfield of three for the Patriots. Starting running back Rhamondre Stevenson rushed for 36 yards across 14 carries, including a not-down-yet long of 12. Meanwhile, Corey Kiner broke off a kickoff return of 38 yards and provided more than breather on offense with 11 handoffs for a Patriots-best 57 ground yards. The summer trade acquisition was leaned on late after losing a fumble a Sunday ago. Left tackle returns as trio of starters depart from offensive line The knee injury that took Will Campbell out in the midst of a 45-17 win over the Las Vegas Raiders did not take him out one Sunday later. The No. 4 overall pick in last year’s class stayed in for every snap at left tackle despite being a questionable call. Three others were unable to do the same for the Patriots’ starting five. Attrition reached a critical mass. Left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker was ruled out due to a hamstring injury sustained in the second quarter. An ankle injury sustained by in right tackle Morgan Moses preceded it. The 35-year-old captain also did not return . And in the final quarter, right guard Ben Brown needed assistance getting off the field due to a knee injury after he had flipped to the other side of the line. In turn, rookie first-rounder Caleb Lomu went from reporting as an eligible tight end to playing bookend while recent 53-man additions Matt Pryor and Walter Rouse stepped on at the guard spots abutting center Jared Wilson. Extra time was fought for by a patchwork offensive line that conceded zero sacks and zero penalties. Smith’s pick-less streak snaps against secondary welcoming back No. 0 A shoulder injury kept Christian Gonzalez sidelined for six practices and two games . But not Sunday. The All-Pro cornerback went without a game designation as part of the starting nickel secondary and helped limit former NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year Garrett Wilson to 44 receiving yards. Jets quarterback Geno Smith completed 20-of-30 passes for 252 yards during the return of No. 0. It marked the veteran’s seventh career start against the Patriots dating back to his rookie introduction in 2013. And it brought one touchdown as well as his initial interception of the campaign. New York’s opening drive stalled on the doorstep of the red zone after 13 plays, 58 yards and a penalty for offensive pass interference that turned a touchdown into a field goal. The next four possessions resulted in a pair of punts and back-to-back turnovers on downs. And by the time halftime hit, the visiting offense had gone 1-of-6 on third down, 0-of-2 on fourth down and 0-of-1 in the red zone while hoarding 19:10 of game clock. But a moon ball behind New England starting safeties Craig Woodson and Kevin Byard III found the hands of rookie wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. for a 48-yard touchdown to make it a 17-10 game in the third quarter. It went from 17-13 game to a 23-13 game to a 23-16 game to a 26-19 game soon after. Along the way, Charles Woods, who started for a corner depth chart still missing Carlton Davis III because of a neck injury, broke the seal with a pick along the sideline. It went in the books as the first career pick for the 2024 undrafted free agent and 2025 waiver claim. It snapped a streak of 165 passes without a pick by New York’s QB, too. Ponder extends tally to 5.5 sacks in six games Three sacks were in the cards for New England. Milton Williams got his first of the fall to set up a third-and-16 in the first quarter. Christian Barmore followed it up on the ensuing snap to put the uprights as New York’s back and the punt unit on. The defensive tackles had company after halftime on Sunday. Elijah Ponder took down the Jets’ QB on third-and-5 to force a field goal and extend his Patriots high to 5.5 sacks on the year. He had four in all as a rookie. The 2025 UDFA out of Cal Poly started off the edge opposite Dre’Mont Jones and now has at least a half sack in five straight games. The outside linebackers were joined in starting front by the the club’s leading tacklers off the ball. Christian Elliss and captain Robert Spillane, who stood up a fourth-and-1 carry from 6-foot-1, 235-pound running back Braelon Allen, combined for 11 more tackles on Sunday. And another fourth-and-1 halting. The Jets’ running backs managed 94 rushing yards across 24 attempts in the absence of all-purpose threat Breece Hall. Hunter a highlight in the kicking game Patriots kicker Andy Borregales went 2-of-2 on field goals and 2-of-3 on extra points against the Jets, with one try heading wide left. The sophomore split the uprights from 32 yards away in the second quarter and 27 yards away in the fourth quarter. His holder averaged 50 yards per with some help from a rookie linebacker, too. Erick Hunter continued to show up downfield on Sunday. The undrafted linebacker out of Morgan State, who signed in September, downed a 54-yard punt from veteran specialist Mitch Wishnowsky at the opposing three-yard line. The last tackle made by New England’s special teams also went to No. 49, who entered the matchup with six stops in the kicking game.

stories.title: Steelers overcome 16-3 deficit, defeat Buccaneers in OT
stories.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers pull off franchise’s biggest fourth-quarter comeback in 34 years, defeat Bucs to get to 4-2.
stories.detailText: (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images In what is now the franchise’s largest fourth-quarter comeback since 1992, the Pittsburgh Steelers overcame a 16-3 deficit in the final 15 minutes to defeat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers 26-19 in overtime, giving them a 4-2 record and their first win streak of the season. After scoring 30 points in two of their last three contests and showcasing a consistent ability to move the ball, Pittsburgh’s offense was nonexistent through three quarters. Pittsburgh had five three-and-outs and were 5-of-15 on third downs while being limited to just three first half points. However, the offense found life in the fourth quarter. Trailing 16-3, Aaron Rodgers and Germie Bernard led Pittsburgh down the field on an eight-play drive that ended with a Darnell Washington touchdown. Daylen Everette then picked off Jalon Daniels, which led to a Chris Boswell field goal after an eight-play drive that only accumulated 24 yards for Pittsburgh. The Steelers forced a Buccaneers three-and-out which led to a Boswell 58-yard boot to tie the game. Then, Pittsburgh’s defense seemed to potentially seal the game. Jamel Dean picked off Daniels and was shoved out of bounds inside the five yard-line. The Steelers, though, couldn’t punch the ball in the end zone. Rodgers tired to find Washington, but the pass was broken up. A stuffed Jaylen Warren run and an incomplete jump ball to DK Metcalf brought out Boswell for his fourth made field goal of the day. That left over a minute on the clock, though, for the Buccaneers, and Jalon Daniels was able to get enough yards to bring on Chase McLaughlin for his fourth field goal to tie the game at 19 and send it into overtime. The Steelers lost the toss and the Bucs deferred, but Pittsburgh would take full advantage of having the ball first. Rodgers led the offense on a 12-play drive that featured a 3rd-and-13 conversion on a completion to DK Metcalf, who had 11 catches on the day. The drive would culminate with Bernard reaching the end zone for his first career touchdown to put Pittsburgh on top 26-19. After one fourth-down conversion on the Bucs’ ensuing drive, Tampa Bay faced 4th-and-8. Patrick Graham dialed up a Jalen Ramsey nickel blitz, which worked all the way back in the fourth quarter, and it worked again. Ramsey came off the edge untouched and recorded his second sack of the game to seal the win for Pittsburgh. After failing to score a touchdown in the first three quarters, the Steelers scored every time they touched the ball in the fourth quarter and overtime, save for the kneel-down to end regulation. In the process of the comeback, the Steelers may have found their permanent one-two duo at receiver going forward. Both DK Metcalf and Germie Bernard hauled in 11 receptions – the rest of the Steelers’ offense combined for 11 receptions. Rodgers finished the day 33-of-49 for 253 yards and two scores, as well as a first quarter interception. The Steelers will now take their 4-2 record to Paris in Week 7 where they will take on the New Orleans Saints, who recorded their second win of the year by defeating the New York Giants. Let us know what you think in the comments . Be sure to bookmark Behind the Steel Curtain for all the latest news, breakdowns, and more! stories.title: Titans use special teams plays and defense to rally past Colts 26-20 for 1st win of the season
stories.summary: — The Tennessee Titans used a 58-yard punt return to set up their first touchdown Sunday, returned a blocked punt for another score and got a 49-yard field goal from Joey Slye with 2:03 left to earn their first win of the season, 26-20 over the...
stories.detailText: INDIANAPOLIS -- — The Tennessee Titans used a 58-yard punt return to set up their first touchdown Sunday, returned a blocked punt for another score and got a 49-yard field goal from Joey Slye with 2:03 left to earn their first win of the season, 26-20 over the Indianapolis Colts . Tennessee (1-5) ended a six-game losing streak in the series with a relentless defensive effort and two game-changing special teams plays that helped them overcome a 13-0 halftime deficit. Cam Ward was 11 of 22 for 102 yards, with one TD and one interception as Tennessee scored its most points all season. Tony Pollard rushed 19 times for 76 yards and rookie Carnell Tate caught had six catches for 70 yards and his first TD reception. The defense finished with six sacks and three takeaways. Indy (2-4) dominated the first half with a 232-64 edge in total yards, but only produced three scoring drives, settling twice for field goals. The Colts have lost two in a row. Daniel Jones was 22 of 42 for 269 yards with one TD and two more interceptions — both costing the Colts scoring chances. Jonathan Taylor ran 21 times for 94 yards and one score while catching two passes for 57 yards. Keenan Allen had eight catches for 82 yards. Tennessee's rally began with Jeffery Simmons forcing Taylor to fumble on the first play of the second half, which set up a 29-yard field goal. Slye added a 56-yarder with 3:21 to go in the third quarter. Then the Titans' special teams changed the game. Chimere Dike’s long punt return early in the fourth set up Ward's 8-yard TD pass to Tate for the tying score with 13 minutes remaining. After forcing a punt on Indy's next possession, James Williams Sr . broke free and blocked Rigoberto Sanchez 's punt. Oluwafemi Oladejo scooped it up for a 14-yard return that gave the Titans a 20-13 lead. Indy tied the score on Taylor's 4-yard run with 5:32 to go, but a 36-yard pass interference penalty on Colts cornerback Cam Taylor-Britt helped the Titans move into field-goal position for Slye, who added a 44-yard field goal with 43 seconds left after the Colts turned the ball over on downs. Jones got one last chance but couldn't connect on either desperation heave in the waning seconds. Up next Titans: Will try to win their first home game next Sunday against Cleveland. Colts: Begin a two-game road trip next Sunday at Minnesota. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here

stories.title: Steelers pull out 26-19 win over Bucs in overtime
stories.summary: Aaron Rodgers threw a 6-yard touchdown pass to Germie Bernard for the game-winner in overtime.
stories.detailText: Nothing was going right for the Steelers on Sunday. They trailed the Buccaneers 16-3 in the fourth quarter. Pittsburgh won 26-19 in overtime. The Steelers are 4-2 and the Bucs 1-5. The Steelers dominated the fourth quarter, gaining 230 yards and forcing two Jalon Daniels interceptions. Their fourth-quarter scoring drives were 68, 24, 37 and 2 yards. Chris Boswell's 58-yard field goal tied the game 16-16 with 1:55 left. Two plays later, former Bucs cornerback Jamel Dean intercepted Daniels. Dean went 40 yards with the return of the errant pass before Daniels pushed him out of bounds at the Tampa Bay 3. The Steelers couldn't get it into the end zone, but Boswell's 20-yard kick with 1:21 left gave the Steelers their first lead. They left too much time for the Bucs, though, as Tampa Bay needed only a field goal to send the game to overtime. With eight seconds left, Chase McLaughlin kicked a 53-yard field goal to tie it 19-19. It was McLaughlin's fourth field goal of the day, with the others from 43, 47 and 52 yards. The Steelers got the overtime kickoff, and Aaron Rodgers got his seventh overtime win with a 12-play, 70-yard drive that burned 6:45 of the 10-minute period. He threw a 6-yard touchdown pass to Germie Bernard for the game-winner. The Bucs drove across midfield, but on fourth-and-8 with 1:06 remaining, Jalen Ramsey sacked Daniels to end it. Ramsey had two sacks as did Nate Herbig. The Bucs sacked Rodgers five times and frustrated him for most of the game. But he finished 33-of-49 for 253 yards with two touchdowns and an interception. DK Metcalf caught 11 passes for 93 yards, and Bernard had 11 catches for 87 yards and a touchdown. The Steelers outgained the Bucs 300 to 224. Daniels was 22-of-43 for 164 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions.

stories.title: Bryce Young throws for 2 TDs and leads Panthers to 25-14 win over injury-riddled Eagles
stories.summary: — Bryce Young threw for 281 yards and two touchdowns to Tommy Tremble, and Chuba Hubbard ran for 120 yards and a score to lead the Carolina Panthers past the injury-riddled Philadelphia Eagles 25-14 on Sunday.
stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA -- — Bryce Young threw for 281 yards and two touchdowns to Tommy Tremble , and Chuba Hubbard ran for 120 yards and a score to lead the Carolina Panthers past the injury-riddled Philadelphia Eagles 25-14 on Sunday. The Panthers (3-2) had little trouble in the second half picking apart the Eagles (2-4), who were missing quarterback Jalen Hurts and running back Saquon Barkley . Hurts is on injured reserve and will miss at least four games with a blood clot in his calf . Barkley missed his second straight game with a hamstring injury and Will Shipley and Tank Bigsby , his two backups, were also sidelined by injuries. The quarterback showdown between Young and Eagles backup Tanner McKee seemed like a mismatch entering the day. McKee, in his fourth season, made his third career start and first one without the Eagles having already clinched a playoff berth. McKee was sacked for an 11-yard loss on the Eagles’ first play from scrimmage and he nearly had a pass intercepted on second down. The 26-year-old’s outing never got much better, and he finished 26 of 45 for 215 yards and a touchdown. He hit DeVonta Smith — who missed the last two games with a hamstring injury — for a 19-yard TD that pulled the Eagles within 19-14 early in the fourth quarter. The Eagles forced a three-and-out and then wasted their drive when McKee lost 12 yards on a fumble. Young sealed the win with his second TD pass to Tremble, a 19-yarder for a 25-14 lead. Young — who threw a 12-yard TD pass to Tremble in the second quarter — bailed out the Panthers late in the third on third-and-8 at their own 10 when he connected with Jalen Coker for a 32-yard gain. Young extended the drive with a 15-yard completion, and the Panthers converted a fourth-and-1 when Hubbard found a hole for a 19-yard run. Hubbard finished the drive in the fourth with a 2-yard touchdown run for a 19-7 lead. Carolina’s 2-point attempt failed. A week after the Eagles lost by a field goal on the final play against Jacksonville in London, Ryan Fitzgerald made kicks of 47 and 52 yards for the Panthers. The latter made it 13-7 and was his 11th straight successful attempt to open the season. He did miss an extra point. The Eagles are in a world of hurt without Hurts and were forced to turn to McKee, who had lost his grip on the No. 2 spot in training camp. He regained the backup job after the Eagles cut Andy Dalton , but he looked out of place all game. Offensive coordinator Sean Mannion did him no favors by calling a series of failed screen and swing passes. McKee threw a third-and-14 sideline pass for Smith in the third quarter that sailed out of bounds against one of the worst defenses in the NFL and was greeted by boos. The struggling offense isn’t all on McKee. The Eagles were shut out in the third quarter and have scored only six points in that quarter all season. Philadelphia had only 37 total yards in the first quarter and punted on its first five drives. Dameon Pierce scored on a 2-yard run to cut Carolina’s lead to 10-7 at halftime. Injuries Panthers: OLB Jaelan Phillips aggravated a hamstring injury. ... OLB Thomas Incoom suffered a calf injury. Eagles: Edge rusher Nolan Smith left in the first half with a concussion after he absorbed helmet-to-helmet contact with Hubbard. ... RB Carson Steele suffered a shoulder injury. ... DT Jordan Davis injured an ankle. Up next Panthers: Host Tampa Bay next Sunday. Eagles: Host Dallas on Monday, Oct. 26. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here

stories.title: Caleb Williams is back, so is Chicago's hope: Bears vs. Falcons winners, losers
stories.summary: The Bears can resume their championship mission with QB Caleb Williams back from injury in impression fashion.
stories.detailText: ATLANTA – Exhale, Bears fans. Caleb Williams is back. The Bears quarterback returned with aplomb after missing three games with a right hamstring injury . Judging by the eye test and results, he’s pretty close to being all the way back. Williams, 24, led the way to a 31-23 victory against the Atlanta Falcons by passing for 305 yards and a touchdown. He didn’t test the leg much by running out of the pocket (four rushes, 3 yards), but with the flow of the game – Chicago built a 31-7 lead – he didn’t need to leg out a lot. Bottom line, the Bears (4-2) can resume their mission of championship dreams with their most important player back in the fold after rebounding from the most significant injury of his career. Here are the winners and losers from the Bears' victory over the Atlanta, which fell to 2-4. WINNERS Caleb Williams After missing three games as he healed his right hamstring injury, it didn’t take long for the Bears’ star quarterback to confirm his health status. Williams completed his first 12 passes against the Falcons, including a rolling, 14-yard TD strike to Colston Loveland to finish the opening drive as the Bears jumped to a 14-0 lead in the first quarter. Beyond the production, Williams showed no apparent effects from his injury as he moved fluidly on roll-out passes, scrambles and with improvisation to buy time in the pocket. Final analysis: He’s back. Kyler Gordon The Bears’ nickelback is back, too. What a sensational debut for Gordon, who was activated off the PUP list on Saturday after rehabbing from a calf injury. He collected three sacks of Michael Penix Jr., including the strip sack late in the fourth quarter. Gordon, who was limited to just three games last season while dealing with soft-tissue issues, was essentially Chicago’s best pass-rusher on Sunday. He rushed eight times, according to Fox, and on top of the sack hat trick, posted five QB pressures. Jeff Ulbrich As the NFL rolls with its annual – and undeniably worthy – support of Breast Cancer Awareness Month, there’s a special distinction for the Falcons’ defensive coordinator. Ulbrich lost his wife, Christina, 48, to cancer in July . Rather than take an extended leave of absence, Ulbrich opted to continue working despite his personal crisis, and has expressed appreciation for the support from the players on his unit – and people throughout the organization. Before the game on Sunday, Ulbrich walked his usual laps around the field while wearing a T-shirt with the message, “I play for Christina Ulbrich.” And his defense has played better than expected this season despite the absence of the top two pass-rushers – Jalon Walker and James Pearce, Jr. – and the loss of Pro Bowl cornerback A.J. Terrell to a season-ending groin injury. Kendal Daniels The Falcons’ rookie linebacker was carted off the third quarter , strapped to a long backboard, after suffering a neck injury. The game was delayed for several minutes and Mercedes-Benz Stadium became eerily silent as medical personnel tended to Daniels. He was ultimately taken to Grady Memorial Hospital for further examination. The best news: Daniels reportedly had movement in all of his extremities. Kyle Pitts Take him off the milk carton. Atlanta’s tight end scored two TDs to help rally the comeback attempt in the fourth quarter and had a spectacular 29-yard catch, too. That’s three TDs in two games for Pitts, who scored all of zero TDs in the first four games. LOSERS Atlanta’s rep for homefield “advantage” Mercedes-Benz Stadium is undoubtedly one of the NFL’s most vibrant venues. With thumping music, ribbon video board interaction, promotions, live entertainment and more, the team knows how to put on a great show. And shoot, not just for the Falcons games. By several accounts, it was the best venue during the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Yet there was another takeover on Sunday. A Bears takeover, which was not only reflected by thousands wearing the merchandise – I saw so many No. 34 jerseys paying homage to Walter Payton – but also with the noise that came with pro-Chicago crowd cheering after big plays. The Falcons’ fan base has its contingent of loyalists, but too many season ticket holders are prone to sell their seats to visiting fans. With the 49ers, Chiefs and Lions scheduled in the coming weeks, more takeovers loom on the horizon. Xavier Woods The 10-year veteran lost out by not participating. The Bears released one of their “starting” safeties on Saturday when they activated defensive back Kyler Gordon from the PUP list. Zachariah Branch Tough day for the third-round rookie from UGA. Late in the second quarter, Branch muffed a punt at the Falcons’ 10-yard line – recovered by Josh Blackwell – that killed the momentum after Atlanta clawed back into the game and had a chance to mount a potential game-tying drive. Set up at the 10-yard line, the Bears cashed in with D’Andre Swift’s second TD run to make it 21-7. It was also evident that Branch has some support – most notably from star receiver Drake London, who consoled the rookie on the bench immediately after the gaffe. Divine Deablo Atlanta’s inside linebacker, one of his unit’s most consistent players, was knocked out of the game with an arm injury in the second quarter and did not return. Tough break for a defense that was dissected early by Caleb Williams before it settled down to register a few stops. Follow Bell on X: @JarrettBell This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Caleb Williams is back, so is Chicago's hope: Bears vs. Falcons winners, losers

stories.title: Chicago Bears Ground the Atlanta Falcons in Caleb Williams’ Return
stories.summary: The Chicago Bears helped make this one interesting, but they held on to win over the Atlanta Falcons.
stories.detailText: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 18: Michael Penix Jr. #9 of the Atlanta Falcons congratulates Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears after the game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images Hello Chicago Bears fans! Well, I think we were all nervous coming into this week as we tried to forget that terrible afternoon in Lambeau and get our Bears back on track. While that Guy (Kyle Monngai) would be out for the game again, we got back the captain, the Iceman, Caleb Williams, to lead the Bears on the field. And while the Bears had a number of starters, particularly on defense, out for the game, hope blossomed in Georgia. The Chicago Bears controlled this one for three-plus quarters with efficient offense and decisive special-teams play, but then watched the Falcons mount a spirited late rally against backups. The final score landed at 31-23 in favor of the Bears once the clock hit zero. Let’s talk about what happened. First Quarter: Bears Open the Gates Chicago came out sharp. After a methodical 10-play, 67-yard drive, Caleb Williams hit Colston Loveland for a 14-yard touchdown (Cairo Santos kick) to go up 7-0. The Bears then answered their own three-and-out defense with another sustained drive, capped by D’Andre Swift ’s 4-yard plunge. This officiating crew is known for a lot of yellow on the field, and they didn’t disappoint – well, at least if you’re a Falcons fan. More on that topic on this week’s Upon Further Review. Gooch Observation: Williams was surgical early (perfect on the opening series in some accounts), and the red-zone issues that plagued Chicago recently were nowhere to be found. Two trips, two touchdowns. The Bears didn’t just take the lead—they treated Atlanta’s end zone like an open house with free punch (non-alcoholic, of course). Gooch Aside : Hey, Sam. Yes, you, Sam Roush. Could you, I don’t know, NOT mess up horribly in every game you play in? That would be great, thanks. Second Quarter: The Muff That Mattered Atlanta finally got on the board when Michael Penix Jr. found Jahan Dotson for a 13-yard score after a chunk play to Drake London, cutting it to 14-7. Despite the fact that the Bears had dominated on the field (even though the Stripes were throwing flag after flag), this touchdown brought a certain parity to the game belied by the actual play. But, that momentum was brief. The Falcons muffed a punt (Zachariah Branch), and Josh Blackwell (yes, that JOSH BLACKWELL) recovered, and three plays later Swift punched in his second score from 2 yards out. Halftime score: 21-7 Bears . Key moment of the half: The muffed punt. It flipped field position and momentum in one bounce and handed Chicago a short field that became a touchdown. Special teams remain the great equalizer. One clean recovery turned a one-score game back into a comfortable lead. Nothing says “welcome back to reality” like turning a fair-catch attempt into a Bears touchdown. Halftime Observations The striped ones were enforcing the Bears Tax hard in the first half. In particular, missing an obvious leg whip on Swift that was at the point of attack and got the tackle – should have been a 15 yard penalty. Caleb was calm and efficient – destroying every narrative about his play in a half where he decidedly did not use his legs at all. Remember when being a Bears fan meant that 3rd and long was just a down away from the punt? How nice is it not to be chained to that reality anymore? I have to note that my prediction that this game would feature a Colston Loveland breakout game came true – and he almost hit my prop with two touchdowns! I’ll take the one. This Ben Johnson offense with Caleb behind it was dynamic and surprising. Looking back now on the parade of the backups – it is clear BJ stuck with a vanilla approach to protect those QBs and their limitations. With Caleb – we get the full flowering of the Ben Johnson offensive attack – and it flustered the Atlanta Falcons. Allen had the defense rocking. This game was a tour-de-force of the training camp heroes, as Street, Noah Sewell, Lynch, and D’Marco Jackson all made big plays for the Bears on defense. For those wondering if the Bears defense was an illusion after the Pack attack last week, Allen had a resounding response to the contrary. Last note for the half – how much better is it to have Kalif Raymond as a Bear than it is Olamide Zacchaeus. Oz again featured in a number of key drops, and Raymond was dynamic in the return and passing game. Third Quarter: Business as Usual Chicago kept the pedal down. A 7-play, 52-yard drive ended with Roschon Johnson ’s 4-yard touchdown run, pushing the lead to 28-7. The Bears owned the clock and the line of scrimmage. It was as dominant a performance as the Bears had produced against the Eagles and the Jets. This despite a major flag/yardage disparity between what the Stripes called on the Bears and what they called on the Falcons. GOOCH Observation: The running game (Swift + Johnson) was the closer in the red zone, while Williams continued to distribute efficiently. Atlanta’s offense stayed quiet. At this point, the Falcons’ offense looked like it was still looking for the parking lot. The Bears, perhaps looking forward to their short week and the Thursday Night game, began to sub in subs for a defense that had already suffered a number of “outs” for the game, and on offense, Jonah Jackson went out with a hip injury. But it looked like the Bears had the game in the bag – so why not? Well… Fourth Quarter: Santos, Then the Late Spark Cairo Santos drilled a 50-yard field goal early in the quarter to make it 31-7. We’re a clear winner right? Well, the fact is there was still quite a bit of time on the clock. Despite this, Chicago rotated in defensive backups. Penix and the Falcons took advantage: Kyle Pitts caught a 10-yard touchdown (successful 2-point conversion to Branch) to make it 31-15, then a 5-yard throw for another successful 2-point conversion to Drake London – to pull within 31-23. I was sweating. You were sweating. We were all sweating. But a late Penix fumble on a sack (forced by Kyler Gordon, and then recovered by the Bears) helped snuff out any real threat. Kyler Gordon had three sacks – the most sacks by a defensive back since Todd Bell (sidenote: I drafted Todd Bell onto my historical Chicago Bears team that we drafted at WCG this summer). Key moments: Santos’ 50-yarder provided the cushion. The two successful two-point conversions showed Atlanta’s fight, but they came against a second-team defense after the Bears had already built a 24-point lead. Gordon’s sack/fumble was a timely reminder that the starters, and how GREAT is it to have Gordon back as a starter, could still close the door. GOOCH Observation: Williams finished 30-of-36 for 305 yards and a TD (no interceptions). Swift had two short-yardage scores, Loveland contributed the early receiving TD, and Luther Burden led the receivers with 95 yards. Penix threw for three scores but spent most of the day chasing the game. Time of possession heavily favored Chicago until the final stretch. And Kyler, let me just say, for all Chicago Bears fans, ALL IS FORGIVEN AND WELCOME BACK. Final Thoughts The Bears built the lead like a team that wanted to go home early and rest up for the Thursday night tilt against the Patriots, but then they politely held the door open while the Falcons scored a couple of late ones against the understudies and made it a game again. But then the Bears reasserted themselves and again showed what had won them the game in the first place, an efficient, physical, and ultimately comfortable performance on both sides of the ball. As for the striped ones, tune in this week for “Upon Further Review” as I take those dudes to the woodshed. But what did you think about the Bears, now 4-2, and their decisive win against the Falcons? Tell us in the comments below!

stories.title: Aaron Rodgers, Steelers rally for OT win in Tampa as Buccaneers' struggles continue without Baker Mayfield
stories.summary: Jalon Daniels threw two fourth-quarter interceptions on Sunday.
stories.detailText: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers need Baker Mayfield back on the field. The Buccaneers blew a 13-point lead in the fourth quarter and allowed Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers to rally and take the 26-19 win in overtime at Raymond James Stadium on Sunday afternoon. That dropped the Buccaneers to 1-5, and a brutal 0-4 on their home field. Rodgers and the Steelers, who had a look to end the game in regulation, mounted a long drive in overtime that he capped with a 6-yard pass to Germie Bernard for the touchdown. That was Barnard's first career touchdown, too, and eventually gave them the win. Germ! Extension! Six! @oti_germie pic.twitter.com/6AZHDzh8uT — Pittsburgh Steelers (@steelers) October 18, 2026 Jalon Daniels, who stepped in to replace Mayfield in Week 4 , threw two interceptions in the fourth quarter on Sunday. While Daniels guided the team to their first win of the season last week in Dallas, he's now just 1-2 in the first three starts of his career. And the Buccaneers are now almost certainly out of reach of the postseason. Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Basketball league for the 2026-27 NBA season Mayfield went down in the team's loss to the Minnesota Vikings last month after he dislocated his right thumb while throwing an interception. An MRI later revealed no ligament damage, but Mayfield has not played since and could be out as many as six weeks . Daniels got the start the following week, and couldn't quite lead the Buccaneers past the Green Bay Packers. He threw two interceptions in that outing, which was his first NFL. But last week, Daniels and the Buccaneers rolled to a win over the Dallas Cowboys behind a huge night from Bucky Irving. At least briefly on Sunday, it looked like Daniels and the Buccaneers were going to pick up right where they left off. They took a 13-3 lead into the locker room at halftime, and Daniels found Emeka Egbuka for a 2-yard touchdown early on. But after pushing that lead to 13 points after a Chase McLaughlin field goal in the third quarter, Rodgers and the Steelers started mounting their comeback. Rodgers led the Steelers on their first touchdown drive of the day early in the fourth quarter, and found a wide open Darnell Washington for the score to make it a one-score contest. 8️⃣ ➡️ 8️⃣0️⃣ @AaronRodgers12 | @_Dwfootball11 pic.twitter.com/N1ijxjPU3G — Pittsburgh Steelers (@steelers) October 18, 2026 Then just three plays later, Daniels threw a bad interception right to Daylen Everette. Daniels just threw it up there on third down, which led to an easy field goal for Chris Boswell. That was the 310th made field goal of his career, too, which is the most in team history. Rooks first‼️ @DaylenEverette pic.twitter.com/91uo3Pmg2j — Pittsburgh Steelers (@steelers) October 18, 2026 The Steelers' defense shut Daniels down again after that, and forced a quick punt in less than a minute. Rodgers put the Steelers in scoring position at the two-minute warning, but he took a huge sack on third down to force them to take another field goal. That tied the game up 16-16. Any momentum that Daniels had offensively was long gone by this point. On just his second play after the Boswell field goal, he threw what nearly turned into a pick-six. While looking for Egbuka, Steelers cornerback Jamel Dean jumped the pass and ran it down to the 3-yard line. DON’T MAKE A SCENE‼️ pic.twitter.com/CPVwIyqjet — Pittsburgh Steelers (@steelers) October 18, 2026 Somehow, Rodgers couldn't punch it in from there. The 20-yard chip shot that put them ahead only lasted briefly. Daniels completed his first pass after missing nine straight, and found Ted Hurst for a 22-yard gain to quickly get them into position to drill a 53-yarder to force overtime. But that led to Rodgers' game-winning drive, and the Steelers' final stop to seal their seven-point win. Rodgers went 33-of-49 for 253 yards with two touchdowns and an interception. The Steelers now sit at 4-2. While they are still in great position in the AFC North, the win was much more complicated than it needed to be. They were on the 3-yard line in the fourth quarter, after all, and had to settle for a field goal instead of a game-winning touchdown. Daniels went 22-of-43 for 164 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions. He won't keep the starting job in Tampa for much longer. The reins will be handed back over to Mayfield as soon as he's able to get back onto the field. While Daniels did lead the team to their first win of the season, the Buccaneers are undoubtedly missing Mayfield. Though a playoff push isn't completely out of the question — the San Diego Chargers lost four straight in 1992 and still made the postseason, though they are the only team in NFL history to accomplish that feat — it's going to take a massive turnaround to pull that off. And that'll have to happen quickly.

stories.title: Giants' fourth-quarter comeback falls short in 34-27 loss to Saints
stories.summary: The Giants lost to the New Orleans Saints, 34-27, after they were unable to complete their wild fourth-quarter comeback at MetLife Stadium.
stories.detailText: The Giants lost to the New Orleans Saints, 34-27, after they were unable to complete their wild fourth-quarter comeback at MetLife Stadium. Here are the takeaways... -- There wasn't much to smile about for New York in this one, but for most of the first half it had a lead thanks to Tyrone Tracy Jr. scoring the game's first touchdown in the first quarter. With Cam Skattebo losing touches entering this game because of too many fumbles, Najee Harris was the lead back, although no Giants running back ran the ball effectively. -- Tracy's touchdown actually came through the air after quarterback Jameis Winston threw him a slant pass in the red zone with Tracy doing the rest, evading defenders and diving into the end zone for six. Tracy scored again in the second half (with the game well out of reach) and could be in line for more carries this season. He led all rushers with six carries and 18 yards, forcing the Giants to throw more in the second half. Devin Singletary had 14 yards on four attempts and a catch for 19 yards while Harris was unable to take advantage of his opportunity and picked up two yards on four carries. Skattebo was effectively benched as he did not touch the ball once. -- Leading 10-0 in a bit of an ugly game, New York allowed the Saints to finally get on the board with a minute and 17 seconds left before the half on a 58-yard field goal. On the ensuing kickoff, though, kick returner Charlie Jones fumbled the ball and it was recovered by New Orleans near the red zone. Tyler Shough and the Saints got to the 2-yard line and, on fourth-and-goal with five seconds left, decided to go for it instead of settling for a field goal. That decision worked out with Shough finding Bryce Lance in the end zone for the receiver's first career touchdown. Just like that, the game was tied. -- After halftime, New Orleans started with the ball and quickly scored on a touchdown pass to Alvin Kamara . The 31-yard catch and run score gave the veteran running back more than 5,000 receiving yards as he became the sixth player in NFL history to have 5,000-plus rushing yards and 5,000-plus receiving yards. -- The Saints scored again later in the quarter and this time Shough did it with his legs, running it in from the 1-yard line. A field goal put New Orleans up 27-10 entering the fourth quarter. -- Another touchdown for the Saints in the early goings of the fourth quarter meant they had scored 34 unanswered points and were walking away with the win. With the Giants struggling offensively, head coach John Harbaugh benched Winston (14-of-26 passing for 152 yards and one touchdown against two interceptions) in favor of J.J. McCarthy , who had entered the game earlier briefly for a run. -- Getting his first chance to actually throw the ball, McCarthy aired it out. He did throw an interception but also had a touchdown pass and led the Giants on three separate scoring drives in the fourth quarter for 17 points to get New York back in the game. His touchdown pass went to Isaiah Likely (six receptions for 99 yards and one touchdown), who also caught a two-point conversion. McCarthy and the Giants even had a chance to tie or win the game after marching down the field during the final minutes of the game. On fourth-and-1 from the Saints' 14-yard line with five seconds left in the game, New York wasn't able to convert and its wild comeback attempt failed. Still, McCarthy showed some real promise (11-of-21 passing for 243 yards and one touchdown against one interception; 26 yards on two carries) and had multiple big plays by finding Malik Nabers , who exploded for 165 yards on 12 catches. stories.title: Eagles injuries stack up late against the Panthers
stories.summary: Jordan Davis was the latest Eagles player to leave Sunday’s Week 6 game with an injury.
stories.detailText: Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images | Getty Images As if the Eagles haven’t had big enough issues keeping their players healthy, things got measurably worse for the group near the end of Week 6’s game against the Panthers. At the top of the fourth quarter, DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks were both injured, but Smith was able to return. Shortly after that, Braden Mann had a blocked punt and was injured during the play. And then on the next defensive play, Jordan Davis went down and had to be helped off the field, and eventually helped to the locker room. Davis was pretty quickly ruled out with an ankle injury. Another injury for the Eagles pic.twitter.com/AfqNlnjwVz — John Clark (@JClarkNBCS) October 18, 2026 At this point, it’s almost easier to list players who weren’t injured in Sunday’s game, but alas, here are the guys who were sidelined in some part or seen gimpy after a play. stories.title: Saints survive J.J. McCarthy, Giants in 34-27 win
stories.summary: A furious comeback effort fell short in McCarthy's first extended action as a Giant.
stories.detailText: The Giants looked like they were throwing in the white towel when they turned to J.J. McCarthy at quarterback with the Saints up 34-10 with under 12 minutes to play on Sunday, but it turned out that they were just getting warmed up. McCarthy threw an interception on his first drive, but led the team to 17 points on their next three while the defense kept forcing New Orleans to punt. The last of those punts came with just over a minute left and McCarthy promptly broke free for a 28-yard run into Saints territory. Completions to tight end Isaiah Likely and wide receiver Malik Nabers got the ball to the Saints' 14-yard-line, but a fourth down throw to Likely in the end zone went incomplete. That left the Saints to exhale with a 34-27 win that ended their three-game losing streak. That should make team owner Gayle Benson a bit happier even if it looked like her team might blow it all before the final whistle. The Giants had a 10-0 lead in the first half, but the Saints went into halftime tied at 10 thanks to a field goal, a fumble on the ensuing kickoff and a Tyler Shough touchdown pass with one second left in the second quarter. They kept rolling in the third quarter as Shough threw two more touchdowns and joined the Kendre Miller/Alvin Kamara/C.J. Donaldson running back committee in posting 175 rushing yards. While that was happening, the Giants were either punting or watching Jameis Winston throw two interceptions that may have pushed his run as the starter to the brink. McCarthy went 11-of-21 for 243 yards and a touchdown to Likely and his 243 fourth quarter passing yards are the third-most since 2020. McCarthy's 28-yard scramble also made him the team's leading rusher. Sunday morning brought a report that Najee Harris would supplant Cam Skattebo as the team's top running back, which proved partially correct. Skattebo played a handful of snaps and never touched the ball while Harris joined Tyrone Tracy and Devin Singletary in the backfield. That group was much less successful than the Saints' trio and the Giants offense lacked any skill position players with impact beyond Likely and Nabers. That tandem combined for 18 catches and 264 yards. The big question is whether they'll continue to catch passes from McCarthy in Week 7. The 3-2-1 Giants will be in Houston to face the suddenly surging Texans and it's hard to see much of an argument that Winston offers more upside than his new teammate given how things played out on Sunday and throughout the older quarterback's career. The Saints will head to Paris on Sunday night to prepare for a game against the Steelers and a win in that one would send them into their bye week with a much rosier outlook than they had when this game got underway.

stories.title: Panthers beat up Eagles 25-14
stories.summary: The Eagles played without quarterback Jalen Hurts on Sunday, and they missed him.
stories.detailText: The Eagles played without quarterback Jalen Hurts on Sunday, and they missed him. Philadelphia had 11 drives, with eight ending in punts and another on downs late. The Eagles put together only two scoring drives of 78 and 69 yards. The Panthers ran away with a 25-14 victory. Carolina is 3-2, and Philadelphia is 2-4. Adding injury to insult, the Eagles lost running back Carson Steele (shoulder), defensive tackle Nolan Smith (concussion) and outside linebacker Jordan Davis (ankle) during the game. The Panthers outgained the Eagles 399 to 222 as Chuba Hubbard ran for 120 yards and a touchdown on 28 carries. Bryce Young was 20-of-39 for 281 yards and two touchdowns. Tommy Tremble scored on touchdown catches of 12 and 19 yards. Jalen Coker caught six passes for 97 yards, and Tetairoa McMillan added six receptions for 86 yards. Eagles backup quarterback Tanner McKee went 26-of-45 for 215 yards and a touchdown. Dameon Pierce had 12 carries for 35 yards and a touchdown. DeVonta Smith caught seven passes for 75 yards.

stories.summary: Moses suffered an ankle injury in the second quarter on Sunday.

He was wearing a walking boot on his right foot. Original story 10/18/2026: Morgan Moses exits Jets game with ankle injury in first half New England Patriots offensive tackle Morgan Moses is officially questionable to return to Sunday’s game due to an ankle injury. The offensive tackle suffered the injury to his right ankle in the second quarter on an incompletion downfield. Moses stayed down on the turf and needed attention from the training staff before going to the blue medical tent. After a lengthy stay in the medical tent he departed to the locker room. With the 35-year old sidelined, first-round pick Caleb Lomu was inserted at right tackle. Lomu played 47 snaps last week at left tackle in relief of Will Campbell, but has spent the majority of his Patriots tenure working on the right side. stories.title: Eagles-Panthers final score: Philadelphia loses fourth straight game in very boring fashion
stories.summary: The Birds are 2-4.
stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 18: Bobby Okereke #58 of the Carolina Panthers sacks Tanner McKee #16 of the Philadelphia Eagles during the first quarter at Lincoln Financial Field on October 18, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles are 2-4 after losing to the Carolina Panthers at Lincoln Financial Field on Sunday. Final score: 25 to 14. Well, that game was very boring. It felt like a 2025 redux. The offense, led by Tanner McKee instead of Jalen Hurts, pretty much sucked. The defense kept the Eagles in the game for most of the day … until the dam inevitably broke in the second half. Watching this offense is just so painful. Yes, the Eagles are incredibly injured on that side of the ball. And they had to deal with even more injuries that were sustained during this game. But it’s hard to argue the coaching staff is doing their part to make the most of what they do have. Something needs to change. Next up for the Eagles: a home game against the Dallas Cowboys on Monday Night Football in Week 7. Ugh. We have to stay up late to watch this dreck? Read on for a recap and stay tuned for BGN’s postgame coverage. Also, check me out talking about this game on the PHLY Eagles postgame show. FIRST QUARTER The Panthers won the coin toss and elected to defer to put the Eagles on offense first. The Eagles took over at their own 26-yard line. Tanner McKee immediately got sacked from unblocked pressure on what was supposed to be a play-action pass. Then McKee’s first throw was a little wide of Makai Lemon and the ball bounced off his hands and was nearly picked off. Facing 3rd-and-21, McKee checked down to Dameon Pierce to pick up some yards to set up a punt. 3 plays, zero yards, punt. Probably not a great thing that the offense looked out of sorts and confused what to do on the very first snap! The Panthers took over at their own 39-yard line. They quickly moved into field goal range. Facing 3rd-and-3 from the plus 30-yard line, the Panthers went with a run that resulted in no gain. Good job by the defense to hunker down. Carolina settled for a 47-yard field goal make that bounced off the right upright and in. EAGLES 0, PANTHERS 3. The Eagles took over at their own 22-yard line after Britain Covey muffed the kick return. Facing 3rd-and-13 after an incompeltion where McKee was pressured with Jake Majors losing his battle and a completion to Pierce for a loss, Lemon made a diving grab that was ruled incomplete by replay assist. Looked like it might’ve actually been a grab. But it was well short of the sticks anyway. 3 plays, -3 yards, punt. The Panthers began at their own 16-yard line. Andrew Mukuba gave up a first down completion to Tetairoa McMillan and also got called for illegal contact, which was declined. Nolan Smith picked up his third sack of the season with the tight end releasing him and Bryce Young holding onto the ball for too long. Facing 3rd-and-12, Young aired it out deep but underthrew Darren Waller and the ball bounced off Riq Woolen’s helmet for a stop. Now that’s what I call using your head! Takedown for Nolan 💪 pic.twitter.com/N32mWI4ll1 — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) October 18, 2026 The Eagles took over at their own 11-yard line. Jordan Mailata immediately false started to knock the offense back. But then McKee aired out to DeVonta Smith, who couldn’t make an impressive one-handed grab while being held but drew the pass interference flag. Positive yardage and a first down! A miracle! McKee got the ball to Carson Steele, who made a nice catch and broke a tackle on his first touch of the season … and then got hurt going to the ground. Naturally. Facing 3rd-and-6, McKee rolled right and it looked like he had nothing to work with … but Dontayvion Wicks was able to make a toe-tapping sideline grab for a first down. Then Pierce took the Eagles’ first rushing attempt for nine yards. Then another Pierce carry for nine yards. Then Pierce broke a would-be TFL to run for no gain. Then Pierce dropped a pass in the flat after getting his head turned around a little late. Facing 3rd-and-10, McKee had his hand hit as he threw for an incompletion. Facing 4th-and-10 from plus 42-yard line, the Eagles lined up to punt and tried to draw the Panthers offside. To literally no one’s surprise, it didn’t work. The Panthers declined the delay of game penalty and Braden Mann punted 28 yards to the Panthers’ 14-yard line. Why not just go for it on fourth down? Or even try a field goal from 60-plus. What are those 28 yards really doing for this team? The Panthers took over at their own 14-yard line and instantly picked up 19 yards (only nine away from where the Eagles punted). Facing 3rd-and-6 after two runs, Young’s third down pass was knocked down by Jalen Carter. Another big defensive stop. The Eagles brought pressure on the punt and it looked like Keyshawn James-Newby got a piece of the ball but he was instead flagged for running into the kicker. The Panthers did NOT opt to go for it on 4th-and-1, instead punting for a touchback. The Eagles took over at their own 20-yard line. Facing 3rd-and-4 after a Pierce run was stopped for a three-yard loss, McKee hit Dallas Goedert at the marker for a first down to end the first quarter. 17 plays for 37 yards to start the game for the Eagles’ offense. Scintillating stuff. SECOND QUARTER McKee hit Darius Cooper for a nice 19-yard completion! But it was wiped out by a Johnny Mundt holding penalty. A league-leading three holding penalties by a tight end. Dude stinks and the Eagles have been asking too much of him to be TE2. Facing 3rd-and-12, McKee stepped up against a blitz and well overthrew Wicks. Watching this offense is sooooo boring. Zzzzzzzzzzzz. The Panthers took over at their own 27-yard line. The Panthers needed just two plays to move into Eagles territory. The Panthers had a 23-yard gain negated by an ineligible man downfield penalty, fortunate break for the Eagles’ defense. Facing 3rd-and-10, Young’s throw short of the sticks to Waller was wide and incomplete. Another stop by Vic Fangio’s defense. The Eagles took over at their own 8-yard line. Goedert dropped a would-be first down reception. Then McKee way overthrew his target as Markel Bell got called for holding but the penalty was declined. 3 plays, four yards, punt. Braden Mann shanked the punt, which went for just 23 yards. The Panthers took over at the Eagles’ 35-yard line. Carter batted down another Young pass and Cooper DeJean flew in for a TFL. Facing 3rd-and-10, DeJean was called for a tacky illegal contact penalty. Unfortunate. The Eagles’ defense pressured Young into an incompletion that was clearly intentional grounding. The refs originally stated that Young was out of the pocket but clearly never left it. Upon discussing it further, they finally threw the flag (lol). But then Jordan Davis got called for roughing the passer by getting his hands on Young’s helmet to give the Panthers more yardage after a 17-yard completion. Hardly a late hit but the refs are gonna call that one. The Panthers entered the red zone and Young hit Tommy Tremble for a 12-yard touchdown. Feels like an insurmountable lead? EAGLES 0, PANTHERS 10. Sure looks like Jihaad Campbell is lost here (as usual). https://t.co/ycQ3hv95AO — Deniz Selman (@denizselman33) October 18, 2026 The Eagles took over at their own 22-yard line. McKee hit Goedert over the middle for a first down! Feels like a miracle. A Goedert false start knocked the offense back to 2nd-and-9. Facing 3rd-and-7 after Lemon got lit up on a short catch in the flat, McKee hit DeVonta Smith over the middle for a first down into plus territory! Is this allowed? McKee threw a pass to Darius Cooper that was actually incomplete but the offense was able to get a snap off fast before a challenge! And it was a run for a first down! Good job. Goedert drew a pass interference penalty with the Panthers’ defensive back pulling his pants down to pick up 22 yards to the 3-yard line. Two plays later, Pierce punched it in up the gut for a touchdown! A touchdown?!!? Points?! Wow. Nice 10-play, 78-yard drive for the score. Life! EAGLES 7, PANTHERS 10. DAMEON PIERCE FOR 6️⃣ pic.twitter.com/UAMpaJcXsa — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) October 18, 2026 defensive pASS interference pic.twitter.com/DZbhtnm1QQ — Crossing Broad (@CrossingBroad) October 18, 2026 That 78-yard drive by the Eagles was their longest scoring drive since Week 2. It's only their fourth scoring drive that went further than 70 yards. — Tucker Bagley (@TBagleySports) October 18, 2026 The Panthers took over at their own 20-yard line. Jalen Carter drew a holding penalty to knock the Panthers’ offense back. Facing 3rd-and-15 after Coker dropped a pass, Young side-stepped pressure and delivered a strike to McMillan for a first down. Really good play by the Panthers QB. Facing 3rd-and-10 after Young put the ball in harm’s way (Cooper DeJean nearly had a leaping interception), Young hit Coker short of the marker. Facing 4th-and-1, the Panthers just let the second quarter expire. Sirianni didn’t call a timeout, either. A little weird that the Panthers wouldn’t try a Hail Mary there. THIRD QUARTER The Panthers took over at their own 30-yard line. Facing 3rd-and-1, the Panthers ran a tight end sneak and picked up the first down. Facing 3rd-and-1 again, the Panthers went with a run that was stopped just short of the marker. Facing 4th-and-inches, Dave Canales threw his challenge flag on the spot. Looked to me like it was indeed a first down. Upon review, the ruling was overturned for a first down. Mukuba missed a tackle to allow a Chuba Hubbard first down run. Then Riq Woolen was flagged for defensive holding to produce another Panthers first down. Facing 3rd-and-10, Fangio brought a blitz and the pressure sped up Young into an incompletion. The Panthers brought in Ryan Fitzgerald for a 52-yard field goal make. EAGLES 7, PANTHERS 13. The Eagles took over at their own 20-yard line after Britain Covey got clotheslined from hell (JBL style) on his kick return and Smael Mondon Jr. got called for holding. Facing 3rd-and-8, McKee was pressured into an incompletion. Inspiring. This game is remarkably boring. — Brandon Lee Gowton (@BrandonGowton) October 18, 2026 The Panthers took over at their own 42-yard line. Facing 3rd-and-1 after two runs, the Panthers were stopped for no gain. The Panthers took a delay of game and punted. Fangio’s defense truly did come to play. The Eagles took over at their own 13-yard line. The Eagles picked up a first down with McKee stepping up against a blitz and hitting Goedert in open space over the middle. Facing 3rd-and-14 after McKee got sacked on play-action, McKee’s pass to DeVonta was high and off target. Hey, five-and-out > three-and-out!!! The Panthers took over at their own 8-yard line after Mann’s punt took a nice bounce out of bounds for 65 yards. Facing 3rd-and-8, the Eagles brought a blitz but Young got it out quick to Coker for a 32-yard catch-and-run. Coker on Baun was not really a great matchup for the Eagles’ defense. Young completed another pass over the middle to former Eagles receiver John Metchie III for a first down into plus territory. Facing 3rd-and-1, the Eagles brought another blitz and Baun pressured Young into a throwaway. Facing 4th-and-1, Canales kept his offense on the field … and Hubbard picked up 19 yards on the ground with Cooper DeJean missing a tackle. Really needed a stop there. The third quarter is finished. The Eagles did not score. They have scored a total of 6 points in the third quarter this season. No other team has fewer than 14 points. The NFL's leader (the Saints) has scored 57 points in third quarters. — Zach Berman (@ZBerm) October 18, 2026 FOURTH QUARTER Facing 3rd-and-9, Young took off running just shy of the marker. Facing 4th-and-inches, Canales kept the offense on the field and the defense jumped on the hard count. How are they doing that with Sirianni obsessed with trying to have his offense get the defense to do that by repping it a good deal in practice? Bad discipline. Two plays later, Hubbard hit the end zone for a touchdown. 14-play, 92-yard TD drive that took 7:43 off the clock to effectively seal the game. The Panthers went for a two-point conversion but failed to convert it. EAGLES 7, PANTHERS 19. 2026 has really been an extension of the 2025 Eagles' season, except worse. Offense sucks, defense keeps the team in it … until getting tired and finally breaking. — Brandon Lee Gowton (@BrandonGowton) October 18, 2026 The Eagles took over at their own 31-yard line. Facing 3rd-and-5, McKee hit Wicks for a 17-yard gain. Wicks was injured after the play. The Eagles went hurry up and picked up another first down. McKee hit DeVonta at the marker for another first down. Or not, he tucked the ball and ran out of bounds before getting beyond the marker. Facing 3rd-and-1, Pierce picked up a first down on the ground. McKee then hit DeVonta for a 19-yard touchdown! Great ball, great catch against tight coverage. Still alive after a 10-play, 69-yard TD drive. EAGLES 13, PANTHERS 19. Welcome back, Smitty 🤌 pic.twitter.com/O5xSoPZK1m — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) October 18, 2026 Eagles run an up tempo Shotgun only drive and score. Who fucking knew? How are they still going under center? How have they not figured this out by now. — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 18, 2026 The Panthers took over at their own 11-yard line after misplaying the kickoff. Baun deflected a Young pass to prevent a completion over the middle for a first down and more. Facing 3rd-and-8, Ty Robinson pushed the pocket and the defense had great coverage to force Young into a throwaway. Big stop! The Eagles took over at their own 48-yard line. Jake Majors had an awful shotgun snap to McKee’s feet for a fumble and 12-yard loss. Facing 3rd-and-18, McKee’s pass to DeVonta was incomplete … but a flag was thrown for pass interference … but McKee’s pass was tipped which took DPI off the table. Unfortunately, the refs missed Tyler Steen taking illegal hands to the face from Derrick Brown. Mann’s punt was blocked (looked like Jeremiah Trotter Jr. missed his assignment) but the ball still went forward for nine yards. The Panthers took over at the Eagles’ 48-yard line. Facing 3rd-and-1, Hubbard gained a first down to the left side. DeJean also got called for unnecessary roughness simply for getting up while a Panthers player was on top of him. Really bad call by the refs. Not sure what DeJean was supposed to do instead. One play later, Young hit Tremble for a 19-yard touchdown. The Panthers’ kicker missed their PAT kick. EAGLES 14, PANTHERS 25. The Eagles took over at their own 13-yard line. The Eagles quickly moved near midfield, aided by a Panthers roughing the passer penalty. McKee hit Lemon for another first down into Panthers territory. But then McKee got sacked by former Eagles edge rusehr Jaelan Phillips to set the offense behind midfield. Facing 3rd-and-17, McKee and Darius Cooper weren’t on the same page with their timing. Facing 4th-and-17, DeVonta almost made a contested catch along the sideline but the Panthers’ backup cornerback knocked the ball out of the receiver’s control. Turnover on downs. Game. The Panthers took over at their own 49-yard line with 4:26 left. The Eagles burned their timeouts as the Panthers picked up a first down. The Panthers moved to 3rd-and-1 from the the 4-yard line and ran for a first down to finish the game by kneeling in goal-to-go. EAGLES LINEUP NOTES Jake Majors, not Drew Kendall, got the start at center. With Kendall not yet fully healthy, the Eagles decided to keep him active as an emergency depth option. Kenny Moore, not Marcus Epps, got the start at safety next to Andrew Mukuba in nickel packages. Darius Cooper lined up as a kick returner with some of the Eagles’ normal options out. Jeremiah Trotter Jr., not Jihaad Campbell, was in at linebacker next to Zack Baun on the Panthers’ third drive. Keyshawn James-Newby took his first NFL snaps on defense with Nolan Smith getting hurt. EAGLES INJURY NEWS DeVonta Smith wasn’t on the field for the Eagles’ second drive. And the start of the third drive. But then he came in. DeVonta got hurt after trying to make a catch in the fourth quarter. He quickly re-entered the game. Carson Steele (shoulder) got hurt on his first touch of the season. He headed to the locker room after being evaluated on the sideline. He was ruled questionable to return. Steele re-entered the game but then got banged up again. He was ultimately ruled out. Nolan Smith (concussion) got banged up in the second quarter. He was promptly ruled out. Jonathan Greenard appeared to be banged up and missed some snaps in the third quarter. Moro Ojomo got banged up in the third quarter. Britain Covey was evaluated after taking a big hit but stayed in the game. Makai Lemon visited the medical tent but remained on the sideline. Cooper DeJean got banged up in the third quarter. Dontayvion Wicks got hurt after a nice catch-and-run. Braden Mann looked banged up after a blocked punt. Jordan Davis (ankle) got banged up in the fourth quarter. He slowly walked to the locker room with a trainer. He was ruled out.

stories.title: Rams' new kicker Blake Grupe forced out with injury just minutes into debut
stories.summary: Latest updates after Rams lose newly signed kicker Blake Grupe to an injury in early setback against the Cardinals in Week 6.
stories.detailText: The Los Angeles Rams might already need another kicker. Blake Grupe , signed this week after Harrison Mevis was booted for missing a potential 48-yard game-winning field goal in overtime against the Buffalo Bills , was called upon Sunday, Oct. 18 to cap off the Rams ' opening drive against the Arizona Cardinals and nailed a 44-yard field goal. On the ensuing kickoff, the 27-year-old out of Notre Dame and Arkansas State lowered his shoulder to push Cardinals kick returner Devin Duvernay out of bounds at the 47-yard line. Grupe stayed down on all fours after the play, visibly in pain, and had to be helped off the field by the training staff. Fox later reported on the broadcast that Grupe went into the blue medical tent before heading back to the locker room, where he remains. He is doubtful to return with a knee injury. Who is the Rams' emergency kicker? Rams punter Ethan Evans was spotted on the sideline kicking into the net as Grupe headed to the locker room. He's never attempted a field goal in his NFL career. He does have experience as a placekicker in college, however, where he went 10-for-18 at Wingate University and hit a career-long 41-yarder on Nov. 5, 2022. NFL teams rarely carry two kickers on a roster, so in cases like this, an emergency kicker is usually called upon. Evans will likely kick if necessary, but Grupe's absence will almost surely make McVay more aggressive when his offense is in field goal range. Rams' two-point conversion attempt almost ends in disaster McVay's aforementioned aggressiveness wasted no time in showing up with the Rams going for two following a 15-yard touchdown pass from Matthew Stafford to Blake Corum rather than letting Evans take the PAT. Stafford stood in the pocket, trying to find a way to get the ball to Devontae Adams on the back pylon until he got rocked on a blindside sack from Josh Sweat that forced a fumble. Cardinals D-lineman LJ Collier scooped the ball up and ran it all the way down to the Rams' 35-yard line before Jordan Whittington made a diving tackle to save LA from giving up the two points to Arizona. The 2-point attempt goes sideways for the Rams as the @AZCardinals get to Stafford and force the fumble! 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/rWrerxj3mW — FOX Sports: NFL (@NFLonFOX) October 18, 2026 This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Rams' new kicker Blake Grupe forced out with injury just minutes into debut

stories.detailText: The Rams special teams are — and have been — a mess. One of the group’s first opportunities on Sunday made things even more complicated. After making his first field goal with Los Angeles, Blake Grupe was injured while trying to make a tackle on a kickoff return. The Rams did not cover the kick well, with returner Devin Duvernay nearly getting to midfield before Grupe hit him to drive him out of bounds. But Grupe suffered a knee injury on the play and is now doubtful to return. According to multiple reporters on the scene, punter Ethan Evans has been practicing kicks into the net on the sideline.

stories.title: Panthers vs Eagles: Recap and analysis
stories.summary: The Carolina Panthers played through a referee show to pull off a road win over the depleted Philadelphia Eagles.
stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 18: Tommy Tremble #82 of the Carolina Panthers celebrates his touchdown with Jalen Coker #18 against the Philadelphia Eagles in the second quarter at Lincoln Financial Field on October 18, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Carolina Panthers played through a referee show to pull off a road win over the depleted Philadelphia Eagles, 25-14. First Quarter The Panthers defense was on the field first and got off to a strong start. Bobby Okereke sacked Tanner McKee on the first play and then nearly intercepted him on the second. The Eagles punted away, and a strong return by Trevor Etienne in his return set the Panthers up with good field position. Chuba Hubbard picked up a first down with his first carry, then Bryce Young hit Tetairoa McMillan a couple times to quickly move into field goal range. The drive stalled out and Dave Canales elected to kick a field goal on 4th and 4 seemingly anticipating a defensive struggle. Both teams exchanged a couple of ineffective drives that ended in punts. The quarter ended with the Eagles…I guess you could call it “driving” on the own side of their field. Second Quarter That drive almost moved when Tanner McKee completed an intermediate pass to DeVonta Smith, but it was called back for a holding in the backfield. That drive also ended a punt. Young completed a couple of passes to Jalen Coker to move the Panthers into Eagles territory. It looked like they had another big play to Mitchell Evans, but it was called back for a very inconsequential ineligible player down field call on Robert Hunt. A couple incompletions later, another punt. The defense forced another punt, and the punt was tipped and went out of bounds at the 35 yard line. The offense responded by picking up a first down via an Eagles penalty. On the next play, Young was not called for an intentional grounding (twice), and then after some complaining, the officials discussed and changed their mind and threw a flag like three minutes later. Young responded by completing a pass to McMillan while benefiting from a roughing the passer penalty going the other way. On the next play, Young found Tommy Tremble wide open in the flat and he took it to the end zone to put the Panthers up 10-0. The Eagles responded with a solid drive of their own. They were aided by a catch on what should have been an incomplete pass, but Dave Canales wasn’t able to get the challenge flag out quick enough. Two plays later, Will Lee was called for a phantom pass interference in the end zone. Another two plays later, Dameon Pierce punched it in. David Moore returned the kickoff out to midfield, but nothing eventful could happen in this game without a flag. The return was called back for a hold. On the next play, Chuba Hubbard’s nice run was called back for a hold. On the next play, the Panthers were called for ineligible players down field, but that one was declined. Young found Tetairoa McMillan to pick up a first down either way. Dave Canales turtled from there and elected to let the clock run out. Neither team called any timeouts, and the game went into the half with the Panthers holding a 10-7 lead. Third Quarter The Panthers picked up a couple of first downs on the first drive. One needed a Canales challenge to get the spot moved to a first down. The offense couldn’t muster more than that, but they did give Ryan Fitzgerald a chance to convert a 52 yard field goal to put the visitors up 13-7. The defense held the Eagles to another punt, but the offense stalled out around midfield once again. Devin Lloyd sacked Tanner McKee on the Eagles next possession while Will Lee had a couple of really nice coverage reps against DeVonta Smith to force yet another punt. The Panthers got backed into the shadow of the end zone, but Young found Jalen Coker breaking free in the middle of the field, and he scooted away for a 32 yard gain. Coker picked up another decent gain later in the drive, and Chuba Hubbard had a few hard runs. One of those came on a 4th and 1 to extend the drive into the fourth quarter. Fourth Quarter Young scrambled to the two yard line to bring up another 4th and 1. The offense stayed on the field, and Young was able to get them to jump on a hard count. Two plays later, Hubbard strolled off the left side for a touchdown. The offense stayed on the field for a 2-point conversion, but Young’s pass was knocked away. The Panthers eased off defensively, and that gave Tanner McKee the space to orchestrate a long drive without taking too much time. Devonta Smith briefly left the game after a hard fall, but he returned to catch a long touchdown over Will Lee. The Panthers bungled the kickoff and ended up deep in their own territory. The offense did nothing, then Sam Martin botched the punt. It looked like things were unraveling for Carolina, but the Eagles came to the rescue. A bad snap on first down put the Eagles way behind the sticks. The defense forced a punt, and Anthony Tyus broke through the line to block the punt. The offense finally took advantage of the field position. They picked up a first down with a Hubbard run, and an unnecessary roughness penalty tacked on more yardage. On the next play, Young found Tommy Tremble completely uncovered down the field for a touchdown. Tremble was called for taunting because he had the audacity to point in the general direction of an Eagles player. Ryan Fitzgerald missed the long extra point. The Panthers defense let the Eagles start moving the ball again, but Ejiro Evero dialed up the pressure when the Eagles got to midfield. Tre’von Moehrig notched a sack. On fourth down, McKee launched a jump ball to Smith, but Zaire Wheatley was able to range over and break up the pass. Chuba Hubbard grinded out a first down then David Moore took a bubble screen 27 yards inside the 15 yard line. One more first down run from Hubbard iced the game. Overview It was far from pretty, but a win is a win. The Panthers set a franchise record for penalty yardage in a game (149) but were able to overcome that and put up a solid 25 points against a vaunted Eagles defense. Chuba Hubbard had an admirable workhorse performance with 28 carries for 120 yards, and Bryce Young put together a quiet 281 yards passing, even if the completion percentage wasn’t great. On defense, Will Lee IV did a very good job on DeVonta Smith, who was basically the only offensive weapon the Eagles had left. The group did what they should have done against an opponent with a makeshift offensive line and dearth of play makers. They limited the Eagles to just 3.6 yards per play. The penalties are really the only thing that kept the Eagles in the game. The Panthers move to 3-2 with the win. They’ll try to keep that momentum going when they host the division rival Buccaneers next Sunday.
